entries.title: Generative image editing
quotes: Delos is to be an image editing tool focused on combining existing content with generative content.
By generative content, we mean both AI-generated content and traditionally generative content, using classical procedural generation algorithms.

sections.Status: Partial. Existing content (imports) and procedural content (seven generators) are combined through operators. There is no AI-generated content: the spec itself defers it ([N6](03-operators.md#n6)).
sections.Implemented by:
- Existing content: the `StaticImage` node kind ([basic.rs:62-95](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L62)), created by `finish_import`, which adds the image and its node with `add_image` and `add_node` ([mod.rs:251-263](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L251)).
- Procedural content: the `Generator` node kinds, registered in `kinds` ([generators.rs:218-220](../../src/nodes/generators.rs#L218)).
- Combination: every node kind is listed in the `REGISTRY` ([nodes/mod.rs:251-259](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L251)); combining kinds report `combines_inputs` ([nodes/mod.rs:236-240](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L236)).
sections.Notes: The project README (Known gaps) names "the cached-source pattern used by background removal" as the intended hook for an AI generator; that pattern is the `Cache` ([cache.rs:1-15](../../src/engine/cache.rs#L1)).

entries.title: Written in Rust
quotes: Delos must be built using the Rust programming language.

sections.Implemented by: - The crate manifest declares `edition` 2024 ([Cargo.toml:4](../../Cargo.toml#L4)). Everything under `src/` is Rust; WGSL kernels are embedded as string constants such as `WGSL_PRELUDE` ([kernels.rs:105-144](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L105)).

entries.title: Desktop, web and mobile with Dioxus
quotes: Delos must be possible to run as a desktop application, a web-based application and a mobile application.
We would like to use Dioxus as our framework for this purpose.

sections.Status: Partial. One Dioxus UI serves all three targets through Cargo features, but the targets are not equal: the web build has no GPU, no threads, no projects and no background removal; the mobile build has no file pickers and no background removal, and according to the README it has never been run on a device.
sections.Implemented by:
- Cargo features `desktop`, `mobile` and `web` pick the Dioxus renderer; only `desktop` enables `rembg` and `rfd` pickers, and `web` enables neither `native` nor `gpu` ([Cargo.toml:8-10](../../Cargo.toml#L8)).
- `launch` starts the desktop window or the generic Dioxus launcher ([mod.rs:26-38](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L26)).
- Background work runs on threads where `native` is enabled and cooperatively (`spawn_local`) on the web ([worker.rs:417-425](../../src/worker.rs#L417)).
- Frames reach the webview through a custom protocol on native targets and through blob URLs on the web: `frame_url` ([platform.rs:53-65](../../src/ui/platform.rs#L53)).
sections.Tests: None. Every test runs the native (desktop) configuration.
sections.Notes: The platform gaps are listed in [D-PLAT](findings.md#d-plat). Only the project gaps are explicitly accepted by the spec ([X3](04-sessions-and-projects.md#x3)); the GPU, threading and background-removal gaps are not mentioned in it.

entries.title: GPU acceleration wherever possible
quotes: Delos will extensively display and manipulate images.
Using GPU acceleration wherever possible is a requirement for this project.

sections.Status: Partial. Every per-pixel kernel has a GPU (wgpu) version, and source images are kept resident on the GPU. Fourier resampling, the background-removal network, banded export encoding and the whole web build run on the CPU only.
sections.Implemented by:
- Kernels are written twice, WGSL and Rust, with one parameter layout; see the `Kernel` struct ([kernels.rs:18-25](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L18)) and the list `ALL` ([kernels.rs:978-980](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L978)).
- `Ctx::kernel` dispatches to the GPU when `active_gpu` is available and the tiles fit, and keeps results on the GPU as `Tile::Gpu` ([engine/mod.rs:283-309](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L283)).
- Source images are sampled on the GPU from resident pyramid levels by `source_on_gpu` ([engine/mod.rs:257-271](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L257)); the levels are uploaded on a background thread (`upload_loop`) that `Resident::new` spawns ([resident.rs:113-116](../../src/engine/resident.rs#L113)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::gpu_matches_cpu`, `tests/split.rs::gpu_split_matches_cpu`, `tests/resident.rs::gpu_sampling_matches_cpu`. `tests/kernel_profile.rs::kernels_on_cpu_and_gpu` times both backends but is an ignored benchmark.
sections.Notes: The CPU-only steps: `fourier_resample` ([resize.rs:126-183](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L126)) and the background-removal `compute_mask` ([bgremove.rs:101-139](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L101)), both reached through `to_cpu`. See [D-PLAT](findings.md#d-plat) for the web build.

entries.title: Graceful CPU fallback
quotes: However, in case GPU acceleration is not available, Delos should degrade gracefully to CPU rendering.

sections.Status: Implemented. The fallback works at four levels: no adapter, a kernel that does not compile, a device error during the session, and a tile larger than the GPU's texture limit.
sections.Implemented by:
- `Gpu::new` returns `None` when `DELOS_NO_GPU` is set, when no adapter exists, or when initialisation fails or panics ([gpu.rs:91-109](../../src/engine/gpu.rs#L91)); software adapters are refused in `init` ([gpu.rs:117-119](../../src/engine/gpu.rs#L117)).
- A kernel whose WGSL fails validation is cached as `None` by `pipeline` and runs on the CPU ([gpu.rs:221-250](../../src/engine/gpu.rs#L221)).
- A device error sets `failed`, so `healthy` turns false ([gpu.rs:134-137](../../src/engine/gpu.rs#L134)) and `active_gpu` stops returning the GPU ([engine/mod.rs:146](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L146)).
- Tiles beyond `max_dim` are not sent to the GPU: `fits` ([gpu.rs:217-219](../../src/engine/gpu.rs#L217)), checked in `Ctx::kernel` ([engine/mod.rs:284-289](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L284)).
- The CPU path of `Ctx::kernel` runs `run_cpu` ([engine/mod.rs:311-323](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L311)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::gpu_matches_cpu`, `tests/gpu_pool.rs::reused_textures_do_not_leak_stale_pixels`, `tests/resident.rs::gpu_sampling_matches_cpu`. The large-image tests run both backends: `tests/large_images.rs::preview_16k_is_interactive`.
sections.Notes: The toolbar badge shows `backend_name` and toggles `use_gpu` at run time ([mod.rs:429-443](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L429)); `active_gpu` returns no GPU while `use_gpu` is off ([engine/mod.rs:143-145](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L143)). The spec asks only for the automatic fallback. Graceful means the same pixels: the parity tests compare every kernel on both backends. The fallback *paths* (compile failure, device loss) are not exercised by any test.

entries.title: Load and display images as graph nodes
quotes: Delos must be able to load and display existing images.
Opening an image creates a "layer" containing that image.
Layers are treated as graph nodes which can be connected using "operators".

sections.Implemented by:
- Decoding goes through the `Codec` registry (`decode` picks the first codec that recognises the bytes) ([formats.rs:183-186](../../src/formats.rs#L183)). PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF and ICO are listed in `CODECS` ([formats.rs:152-164](../../src/formats.rs#L152)).
- `Worker::import` reads and `decode`s the bytes in the background and builds a `SourceImage` with its mip pyramid, which it sends back as `Msg::Imported` ([worker.rs:248-256](../../src/worker.rs#L248), [worker.rs:266](../../src/worker.rs#L266), [worker.rs:270-277](../../src/worker.rs#L270)); `SourceImage::from_rgba8` premultiplies and builds the levels ([source.rs:43-65](../../src/engine/source.rs#L43)).
- The "layer" is a `StaticImage` node ([basic.rs:62](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L62)) whose `params` hold the image id and size as hidden parameters and whose `render` samples the image ([basic.rs:77-91](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L77)). Nodes are connected by `Graph::connect` ([graph.rs:243-264](../../src/graph.rs#L243)).
- Entry point: the toolbar's Import file input ([mod.rs:344-360](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L344)), through `session::import`, which hands the files to `start_imports` ([session.rs:100-103](../../src/ui/session.rs#L100), [session.rs:119-120](../../src/ui/session.rs#L119)).
sections.Notes: Dropping image files on the window (`ondrop`) also imports them through `session::import` ([mod.rs:86-90](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L86), [mod.rs:102-103](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L102)).

entries.title: Import creates a Static Image connected to the output
quotes: Importing an image to Delos specifically creates a "Static Image" node connected directly to the output.

sections.Implemented by:
- `finish_import` adds the `ids::IMAGE` node and, for `ImportTarget::Output`, connects it to the output's only port with `connect` ([mod.rs:255-268](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L255)). The target enum cites this spec item: `ImportTarget` ([state.rs:68-72](../../src/ui/state.rs#L68)). Image files dropped on the window are imported with `ImportTarget::Output` too (`ondrop`) ([mod.rs:86-90](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L86), [mod.rs:102-103](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L102)).
- The kind's display name is "Static Image": `StaticImage::name` ([basic.rs:68-70](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L68)).
sections.Notes: Connecting replaces whatever fed the output, so importing a second image leaves the first one in the graph but detached, and resets the relocated output and selection (`pinned`, `select`). That follows the clause literally; whether it is the intended experience is a decision ([D-IMPORT](findings.md#d-import)). Imports into a layer stack use `ImportTarget::StackLayer` instead.

entries.title: Operator parameters: WYSIWYG or form
quotes: Operators may have parameters.
In case they do, adding the operator node will allow the user to input the operator parameters either via a WYSIWYG interface or via form inputs.

sections.Status: Implemented. Every parameter has a generated form field; the five kinds of on-canvas control cover the spatial parameters (axes, borders, rectangles, points, canvas size).
sections.Implemented by:
- Parameters are declared as `ParamDef` values ([nodes/mod.rs:76-85](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L76)) of a few `ParamKind`s ([nodes/mod.rs:53-66](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L53)); on-canvas controls as `Overlay` values ([nodes/mod.rs:170-182](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L170)).
- `App::add_node` selects the new node ([state.rs:487](../../src/ui/state.rs#L487)), so the inspector's `NodePanel` shows its parameters ([inspector.rs:189-198](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L189)), rendered per kind by `ParamField` ([inspector.rs:249-401](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L249)).
- The image view draws and drags each `Overlay` in `render_overlay` ([image_view.rs:370-510](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L370)); drags write parameters with `set_param`, and the canvas corner writes `canvas_w`/`canvas_h` ([image_view.rs:245-286](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L245)).
sections.Tests: None for the forms or overlays (UI rendering is not tested).
sections.Notes: Which nodes get WYSIWYG controls: Reflection (axis), Clip and Rectangle Split (rectangle), Vertical/Horizontal Split (line), Linear and Radial Gradient (points), and the output canvas of size-less content (corner handle). Fraction parameters show and accept pixels in the form (`ParamKind::Fraction`), converted with the extent of the space the controls live in.

entries.title: The document is a DAG
quotes: While an image is being edited in Delos, we will be able to visualize the final results.
During the process of editing, however, the image will be stored as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) representing image layers and operations applied to them.
That way, we can easily see and modify effects are being applied to which parts of the image.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Graph` holds `nodes`, the `output` node id and the decoded `images` ([graph.rs:66-72](../../src/graph.rs#L66)); edges live on the consumer as `inputs`, an `Option<Link>` per input port ([graph.rs:41](../../src/graph.rs#L41)).
- Acyclicity: `connect` refuses an edge when `depends_on` finds a path back ([graph.rs:255-257](../../src/graph.rs#L255), [graph.rs:224-239](../../src/graph.rs#L224)). Wires drawn in the graph view go through `connect` (`connect_port`) ([graph_view.rs:115-118](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L115)); stack edits check the same with `depends_on` ([graph_view.rs:120-124](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L120)).
- Rendering pulls through the graph: `Ctx::render` asks a node's `render_output`, which renders its inputs through `render_input` ([engine/mod.rs:208](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L208), [engine/mod.rs:219-224](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L219)).
sections.Notes: Some writers set `inputs` directly without the cycle check (`set_stack_layers`, `insert_resize`, the expression builder). They are safe by construction today; the invariants model lists this as fragile spot 2 ([../invariants/findings.md](../invariants/findings.md)).

entries.title: The image view shows what goes to the output
quotes: The image view must show the image that is being sent to the output.

sections.Status: Partial. By default the view shows the output, as specified. A known defect can leave a stale image on screen after an undo or a new document ([D-STALE](findings.md#d-stale)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `App::displayed` falls back to `output` (or the relocated output) as `base` when nothing is selected or the view is locked, and returns it as the `target` ([state.rs:351-356](../../src/ui/state.rs#L351), [state.rs:376-378](../../src/ui/state.rs#L376), [state.rs:385](../../src/ui/state.rs#L385)).
- The image view sends a `PreviewJob` for `d.target` whenever its key changes ([image_view.rs:83-125](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L83)). The worker renders it with latest-request-wins `run_preview` ([worker.rs:179-182](../../src/worker.rs#L179), [worker.rs:208-216](../../src/worker.rs#L208)); `pump` accepts only newer frames ([mod.rs:134-151](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L134)).
sections.Tests: None for the default view (no test calls `displayed` without a relocation or selection). Rendering itself: `tests/engine.rs::invert_and_stack`.
sections.Notes: The preview key is the structural hash of the target, so edits that do not change the shown image (moving nodes) do not re-render. That hash is also the root of the stale-image defect.

entries.title: Graph view, alone or beside the image view
quotes: We must be able to open a graph view instead of the image view or alongside the image view.
It must also be possible to visualize any part of the graph which produces an image.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Layout` has `Image`, `Split` and `Graph` ([state.rs:11-16](../../src/ui/state.rs#L11)); the toolbar's segmented buttons switch it ([mod.rs:398-402](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L398)) and `Root` sets the `main_class` for the layout and shows one or both panes ([mod.rs:72-77](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L72), [mod.rs:107-115](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L107)).
- Any part of the graph: selecting a node previews it (see [F3.2](#f3-2)) and relocating the output pins it (see [F3.1](#f3-1)).

entries.title: Relocating the output
quotes: In other terms, we can temporarily relocate the output to any image node.

sections.Implemented by:
- The relocated output is `App::pinned`, an `Option<Link>` ([state.rs:114-115](../../src/ui/state.rs#L114)); `displayed` uses it as the `base` while it names an existing output (`has_link`) ([state.rs:351-356](../../src/ui/state.rs#L351)).
- Ways to set `pinned`: double-click in the graph view ([F3.1.1](#f3-1-1)) and the inspector's "View as output" buttons ([inspector.rs:131-153](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L131)). The toolbar badge's Reset clears `pinned` ([mod.rs:422](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L422)).
- Undo, redo and deletions drop a `pinned` link that no longer exists: `fix_selection` ([state.rs:291](../../src/ui/state.rs#L291), [state.rs:296-298](../../src/ui/state.rs#L296)), `delete_node` ([state.rs:531-533](../../src/ui/state.rs#L531)).
sections.Notes: "Temporarily": `pinned` is UI state, never saved in the project, and is cleared by `replace_document` when a project is opened or closed.

entries.title: Double-click to relocate and to reset
quotes: Double-clicking a node in the graph view relocates the output to it.
For nodes with several outputs, double-clicking one of its output ports relocates the output to that output.
Double-clicking the relocated node again, or the Output node, moves the output back to its default.

sections.Implemented by:
- The node's `ondoubleclick` toggles `pinned`: the output node or an already relocated node resets it, any other node sets its first output ([graph_view.rs:346-354](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L346)).
- Each output port has its own `ondoubleclick`, which pins `Link::new(id, o)` or resets it if that port is the one shown ([graph_view.rs:367-368](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L367), [graph_view.rs:381-385](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L381)).
sections.Tests: None (graph-view events are not tested; `tests/ui_state.rs::a_split_output_can_be_viewed_and_exported` sets `pinned` directly).
sections.Notes: Double-clicking the *body* of a split relocates to output 0 (`id.into()`), and double-clicking the body of a split pinned on output 1 resets the output instead of switching to output 0.

entries.title: Selecting a node previews it with its controls
quotes: If we select an operator node, the image view should show the image at the operator's output overlaid with controls for the specific operator (examples of controls: selection boxes, rules).
Examples are given in the operators section below.

sections.Implemented by:
- `displayed`, when not locked, targets the selected node and sets `editing` with an identity `overlay_space` ([state.rs:357-365](../../src/ui/state.rs#L357)).
- `ImageView` draws the overlays of the `editing` node ([image_view.rs:159-160](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L159)) with `render_overlay` ([image_view.rs:370-510](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L370)).
- "Preview selection" is the `follow_selection` checkbox ([mod.rs:410-416](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L410)), on by default (`App::new`) ([state.rs:152](../../src/ui/state.rs#L152)).

entries.title: Some operators are edited on their input
quotes: Some operators are edited on their input instead.
For example, Clip shows the uncropped input with the crop rectangle.

sections.Implemented by:
- The `EditView` enum: `Output` or `Input(port)` ([nodes/mod.rs:184-192](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L184)), returned by `NodeKind::edit_view` ([nodes/mod.rs:226-228](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L226)).
- `Clip::edit_view` and `Split::edit_view` return `EditView::Input(0)` ([basic.rs:340-342](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L340), [split.rs:103-106](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L103)).
- `displayed` shows the input link for `EditView::Input` ([state.rs:360-363](../../src/ui/state.rs#L360)); in the locked case it composes the kind's `input_map` so the controls land on the input's space ([state.rs:370-374](../../src/ui/state.rs#L370)).
- The inspector converts fractions with the input's extent for such kinds (`param_extent`) ([inspector.rs:63-71](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L63)).

entries.title: Keep the view fixed while editing upstream
quotes: It must be possible to keep the image view fixed while editing a node further up the graph.
While the output is relocated (or when "Preview selection" is turned off), selecting another node keeps the view as it is and draws that node's controls over the shown image.
Editing those controls modifies the shown image directly.

sections.Implemented by:
- "Preview selection" is the toolbar's `follow_selection` checkbox ([mod.rs:403](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L403), [mod.rs:410-416](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L410)). `displayed` is `locked` when `pinned` is set or `follow_selection` is off; the target stays on `base` and `overlay_space` comes from `Graph::space_map` ([state.rs:356](../../src/ui/state.rs#L356), [state.rs:366-377](../../src/ui/state.rs#L366)).
- The overlays are mapped into the shown image's coordinates through `to_frac` and `frac_to_screen` ([image_view.rs:161-165](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L161)); the mapping is frozen while dragging (`frac_map`) ([image_view.rs:38-41](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L38)).
- A drag writes the upstream node's parameters (`set_param`, `edit_coalesced`); the shown image's hash changes and it is re-rendered ([image_view.rs:245-276](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L245)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::space_map_follows_geometry_upstream` (the mapping). The locked UI path has no test.
sections.Notes: The edit `badge` says "Editing X · showing Y" ([image_view.rs:171-172](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L171)).

entries.title: Controls follow geometry through intermediate nodes
quotes: Controls must be placed correctly even when nodes between the edited node and the shown image move or scale pixels (Clip, Resize, Downscale, …).
Every node type describes how it maps coordinates to its inputs, so new node types can take part.

sections.Status: Partial. Clip, Resize and Downscale describe their maps, and `space_map` composes them. The map model is a separable affine map along one path, so two cases are not handled: a node whose map is not affine (Reflection folds the image), and an edited node that reaches the shown image along several paths with different geometry, where only the first path is used ([D-OVERLAY](findings.md#d-overlay)).
sections.Implemented by:
- The extension point: `NodeKind::input_map`, defaulting to an identity, top-left aligned map ([nodes/mod.rs:229-235](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L229)).
- Overrides: `Clip::input_map` (offset) ([basic.rs:343-348](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L343)), `Resize::input_map` (scale, using the rounded effective factor) ([resize.rs:73-81](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L73)), `Downscale::input_map` ([resize.rs:238-245](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L238)).
- Composition: `Graph::space_map` and `space_map_rec` walk the inputs depth-first, compose `Map2`s with `after`, and return the first path that reaches the edited node ([graph.rs:313-343](../../src/graph.rs#L313)).
- `Map2` is separable (no rotation or shear) ([geom.rs:95-102](../../src/engine/geom.rs#L95)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::space_map_follows_geometry_upstream`. `tests/engine.rs::clip_offsets_input` checks the rendered pixels, which supports the note below.
sections.Notes: Renders use the same `input_map` (Clip, Resize and Downscale call it from `render`), so the overlay mapping and the pixels cannot disagree for these kinds.

entries.title: Say so when the selected node does not contribute
quotes: If the selected node does not contribute to the shown image, the view says so instead of showing controls.

sections.Implemented by:
- `space_map` returns `None` when the node does not feed the shown one, so `overlay_space` is `None` ([state.rs:368](../../src/ui/state.rs#L368), [state.rs:376](../../src/ui/state.rs#L376)).
- With no `overlay_space`, no overlays are drawn and the badge reads "X does not feed Y · double-click it in the graph to view it" (`badge`) ([image_view.rs:159-160](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L159), [image_view.rs:171](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L171), [image_view.rs:173](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L173)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::space_map_follows_geometry_upstream` asserts `space_map` is `None` for a node that does not feed the output. The badge is untested.

entries.title: Export any operator's output; export the visible image by default
quotes: It must be possible to export the image output by any Delos image operator, but by default the easiest operation to perform should be to export the output currently visible in image view.

sections.Status: Partial. Any operator's output can be exported, and the default is the visible image, with one deliberate exception: while a node edited on its input (Clip, splits) is previewed, the default export is that node's output, not the input shown on screen ([D-EXPORT-TARGET](findings.md#d-export-target)).
sections.Implemented by:
- Default: the toolbar's Export button and ⌘E call `open_export(None)` ([mod.rs:387-393](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L387), [mod.rs:294](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L294)), which exports `displayed().export_target` ([state.rs:392-397](../../src/ui/state.rs#L392)) by opening the dialog on that `target` (`ExportState`) ([state.rs:407-408](../../src/ui/state.rs#L407)).
- Any operator: every non-output node's inspector has one Export button; for a split it exports the output being viewed, else output 0 (`export_link`) ([inspector.rs:87-90](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L87), [inspector.rs:154](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L154)). To export a split's second output, view it first.
- `export_target` is the edited node when not locked, else the shown target ([state.rs:380](../../src/ui/state.rs#L380)).
sections.Tests: None for the default target or the inspector button; `tests/ui_state.rs::a_split_output_can_be_viewed_and_exported` covers the relocated case ([F4.1](#f4-1)).

entries.title: Export follows the relocated output
quotes: While the output is relocated, exporting the current image will export the content of the node that is currently attached to output.

sections.Implemented by:
- When `pinned` is set, `displayed` is `locked` and `export_target` is the pinned link, returned in `Displayed` ([state.rs:353-354](../../src/ui/state.rs#L353), [state.rs:356](../../src/ui/state.rs#L356), [state.rs:380](../../src/ui/state.rs#L380), [state.rs:385](../../src/ui/state.rs#L385)).
- The export job carries that `Link`, so a split's specific output is exported: `ExportJob` ([worker.rs:28](../../src/worker.rs#L28), [worker.rs:31](../../src/worker.rs#L31)).

entries.title: Banded, bounded, cancellable export and its dialog
quotes: Export renders at full resolution in bands (to bound memory), shows progress and can be cancelled.
The export dialog can be closed with its close button, the Escape key or by clicking outside it, and closes by itself after a successful export.

sections.Status: Partial. Rendering is banded for every format, but only the PNG encoder streams bands. The other encoders collect the whole RGBA8 image before encoding, and exports to memory (the web, and the mobile fallback) hold the whole encoded file, so memory is bounded only for PNG written to a file ([D-EXPORT-MEMORY](findings.md#d-export-memory)). The dialog behaviour is as specified.
sections.Implemented by:
- Bands: `GraphBands::new` picks about 4 Mpx per band and `next_band` renders each with `exact` requests ([formats.rs:230-233](../../src/formats.rs#L230), [formats.rs:244-256](../../src/formats.rs#L244)). On native targets `export` renders on another thread with a one-band channel; elsewhere bands render inline ([formats.rs:259-300](../../src/formats.rs#L259)). `ExportDest::Memory` collects the encoded file in a `Vec` ([worker.rs:311-315](../../src/worker.rs#L311)).
- Streaming PNG: `Png::encode` writes each band to a `stream_writer` ([formats.rs:135-149](../../src/formats.rs#L135)).
- Progress: `Prefetched::next_band` reports the fraction ([formats.rs:320-327](../../src/formats.rs#L320)), forwarded as `Msg::ExportProgress` by the `progress` callback that `Worker::export` passes to `formats::export` ([worker.rs:289-291](../../src/worker.rs#L289), [worker.rs:303](../../src/worker.rs#L303)), stored by `pump` ([mod.rs:188-193](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L188), [mod.rs:197-198](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L197)) and drawn as a `progress` bar ([dialogs.rs:170-173](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L170)).
- Cancel: `Worker::export` registers a `cancel_flag` per job and passes it as `cancel` ([worker.rs:281-282](../../src/worker.rs#L281), [worker.rs:287](../../src/worker.rs#L287)); `cancel_export` sets the job's flag ([worker.rs:392-396](../../src/worker.rs#L392)), which `Ctx::render` and `Ctx::kernel` check through `cancelled` and stop with `Cancelled` ([engine/mod.rs:179-181](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L179), [engine/mod.rs:201-203](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L201), [engine/mod.rs:275-277](../../src/engine/mod.rs#L275)); a partial file is deleted (`remove_file`) ([worker.rs:304-307](../../src/worker.rs#L304)).
- Closing: the × button and Close, both `export.set(None)` ([dialogs.rs:124-126](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L124), [dialogs.rs:194](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L194)), `Key::Escape` when no export runs ([mod.rs:297-304](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L297)), a click on the backdrop that also started there (`export_backdrop_clicked`) ([state.rs:436-440](../../src/ui/state.rs#L436)). `pump` closes the dialog after `ExportDone` succeeds ([mod.rs:199](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L199), [mod.rs:207-210](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L207)).
sections.Notes: The shortfall: other formats go through `ImageCrate::encode`, which appends every band to `all` first ([formats.rs:83-88](../../src/formats.rs#L83)).

entries.title: Combination through operators, with display modalities
quotes: All combinations of images will be done using operators.
For example, rather than stacking layers by default, Delos should make it possible to combine layers with specific operators.

Delos shall define specific "display modalities" for standard operators to make user experience more pleasurable - for example, if we combine a sequence of layers using the "stack" operator, we can display this as a layer stack rather than as a degenerate graph of the format `(layer3 STACK (layer2 STACK layer1))` (i.e. a Lisp list of stacks, with the exception that it will never be empty hence a NIL-node is not required.)

sections.Status: Partial. All combination is done by operator nodes, and the layer stack has its display modality in the graph view, the inspector and the expression format. No other operator has one: the spec says modalities (plural) for standard operators, but only gives the stack as an example ([D-MODALITIES](findings.md#d-modalities)).
sections.Implemented by:
- Combining kinds are ordinary nodes (`Stack`, `Blend`) with `combines_inputs` ([basic.rs:114-133](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L114), [basic.rs:213-234](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L213)).
- Chains: `is_interior_stack`, `chain_head` and `stack_chain` recognise a chain of stacks linked through the back port ([graph.rs:426-465](../../src/graph.rs#L426)); `set_stack_layers` rewrites it from a layer list ([graph.rs:470-491](../../src/graph.rs#L470)).
- Graph view: interior stacks are hidden (`is_interior_stack`) and the head shows one row per layer plus "+ add layer" (`stack_chain`) ([graph_view.rs:66-68](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L66), [graph_view.rs:75-87](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L75)); a wire dropped on a row replaces that layer and one dropped on "+ add layer" appends it, through `set_stack_layers` (`connect_port`) ([graph_view.rs:125-132](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L125)).
- Inspector: the `LayerStack` editor lists the chain's layers front to back ([inspector.rs:404-421](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L404), [inspector.rs:439-443](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L439), [inspector.rs:464-468](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L464)).
- Expression format: `(stack front … back)` (see [E4](05-expressions.md#e4)).
sections.Notes: "Never empty": a chain always has at least one stack node (`needed` is at least 1 in `set_stack_layers`), but layers can be empty slots ("+ Empty slot" in the inspector).

entries.title: The basic operator set
quotes: These are basic layer operators which must be implemented in the initial version of Delos:

sections.Implemented by:
- `basic::kinds` lists Output, Static Image, Stack, Disable, Invert, Blend, Reflection and Clip ([basic.rs:10-12](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L10)); `resize::kinds` lists Resize and Downscale ([resize.rs:10-12](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L10)); `bgremove::kinds` lists Background Removal ([bgremove.rs:18-20](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L18)).
- The `REGISTRY` collects them ([nodes/mod.rs:251-259](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L251)); the "Add node" menu lists every `user_creatable` kind by category ([mod.rs:325-332](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L325)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::every_blend_mode_renders`, `tests/engine.rs::invert_and_stack`, `tests/engine.rs::clip_offsets_input`, `tests/engine.rs::reflection_mirrors_pixels`. No test renders Downscale or Background Removal.

entries.title: Stack: over-compositing of a front/back chain
quotes: Stack operator - this is a basic operator which is used to form layer stacks.
A layer stack will be internally represented as `(frontmost STACK (second-frontmost STACK (third-frontmost STACK ... (second-backmost STACK last) ... )))`.
A layer stack will show the first non-transparent pixel found along the stack for each position.
Delos implements this as standard "over" alpha compositing: this matches the rule for opaque pixels and also handles partly transparent ones.
Takes no parameters.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Stack` has the inputs `front` and `back` and no `params` ([basic.rs:114-116](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L114)). A chain links each stack's `back` to the next stack ([graph.rs:441-465](../../src/graph.rs#L441)).
- `Stack::render` returns one side when the other is clear, else runs `OVER` ([basic.rs:120-130](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L120)); `OVER` is Porter-Duff over on premultiplied pixels, front over back ([kernels.rs:228-242](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L228)).
sections.Notes: `Stack::size` is the union of the input sizes, top-left aligned (`union_size`) ([basic.rs:117-119](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L117), [basic.rs:20-24](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L20)).

entries.title: Editing a stack: disable, remove
quotes: If the stack operator is selected it should allow editing the stack, for example temporarily disabling inputs (which will be internally represented as a "Disable" operator which changes all pixels to transparent) or removing them completely.

sections.Status: Implemented. Layers can also be reordered and added (image, generator, empty slot).
sections.Implemented by:
- `LayerStack` in the inspector lists the layers, marking disabled ones (`ids::DISABLE`), and edits them through `set_layers` ([inspector.rs:404-422](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L404), [inspector.rs:428-436](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L428)). The eye button wraps the layer in a new `ids::DISABLE` node or unwraps it ([inspector.rs:444-463](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L444)); ✕ removes the layer from the list ([inspector.rs:483-488](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L483)).
- Every change goes through `set_stack_layers`, which reuses, adds or removes stack nodes and keeps the head's id ([graph.rs:470-491](../../src/graph.rs#L470)).
- In the graph view, removing a layer's edge removes the layer (`disconnect_ref`) ([graph_view.rs:166-174](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L166)).
sections.Notes: Re-enabling deletes the Disable node with `remove_node`. The disabled layer's title is shown greyed (the `enabled` flag). ▲/▼ swap layers (`l.swap`) ([inspector.rs:469-482](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L469)). "+ Image layer", "+ Generator layer…" and "+ Empty slot" add layers (`ImportTarget::StackLayer`, `l.insert`, `l.push`) ([inspector.rs:492-523](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L492)). In the graph view, dropping a wire on a layer row or "+ add layer" edits the chain (`connect_port`) ([graph_view.rs:120-133](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L120)).

entries.title: Disable
quotes: Disable operator - mentioned with stack above.

sections.Implemented by: - `Disable` keeps its input's size (`inputs[0]`) and renders `Tile::Clear` without rendering the input ([basic.rs:156-161](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L156)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::invert_and_stack` (a disabled front layer lets the back layer through). The inspector's toggle is untested.

entries.title: Simple reflection
quotes: Simple reflection operator - this should allow making reflections, i.e. placing axes of reflection on the image which will copy the pixels to one side of them to the other side.
This tool, when selected, will allow (via WYSIWYG rule or form input) selecting where to position the axis of reflection.
Via form, it should allow selecting a vertical or horizontal axis of reflection.
It should also allow specifying whether the reflection should be additive, subtractive or replace the pixels where the reflection will fall.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Reflect::params`: `orientation` (vertical/horizontal; `ORIENTATIONS`) ([basic.rs:241](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L241), [basic.rs:263](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L263)), `position` (a fraction) ([basic.rs:264](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L264)) and `mode` (replace/additive/subtractive; `REFLECT_MODES`) ([basic.rs:243](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L243), [basic.rs:266](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L266)).
- The WYSIWYG rule: `Overlay::Axis` ([basic.rs:272-274](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L272)), drawn and dragged by `render_overlay` ([image_view.rs:384-411](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L384)).
- `Reflect::render` renders the input directly and once more through the `mirror` map, only when the destination interval meets the request ([basic.rs:275-301](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L275)); `REFLECT` picks per pixel and applies the mode ([kernels.rs:290-335](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L290)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::reflection_mirrors_pixels` (replace mode, vertical axis only), `tests/engine.rs::gpu_matches_cpu` (parity, includes additive). Subtractive and the horizontal axis are untested.
sections.Notes: The `side` parameter (copy left→right or right→left; `SIDES`) is not in the spec ([basic.rs:242](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L242), [basic.rs:265](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L265)). Subtractive keeps the destination's alpha; additive clamps in premultiplied space.

entries.title: Downscale
quotes: Downscale operator - should allow for downscaling

sections.Status: Partial. Downscaling works, but "box" is not a box over the chosen factor: below a factor of 2 it samples like nearest, above it uses a fixed power-of-two pyramid level, and size-less inputs are point-sampled ([D-RESIZE](findings.md#d-resize)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `Downscale` with `factor` (1 to 64) ([resize.rs:230-232](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L230)). Its `size` floors the scaled size ([resize.rs:233-237](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L233)); `render` maps the request onto the input with `input_map` ([resize.rs:238-248](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L238), [resize.rs:252-253](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L252)).
- Box averaging comes from the source pyramid: `level_for` picks the level whose texels match the request ([source.rs:114-121](../../src/engine/source.rs#L114)).
sections.Notes: A `method` choice (box average or nearest, `DOWN_METHODS`) is not in the spec ([resize.rs:210](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L210), [resize.rs:231](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L231)); `render` uses `Sampling::Point` for nearest ([resize.rs:249-251](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L249)). For imported images, `level_for` picks the level `floor(log2(step))`, so for steps below 2 it is level 0, sampled nearest ([source.rs:114-133](../../src/engine/source.rs#L114)); above that it samples the chosen power-of-two level bilinearly.

entries.title: Background removal with rembg-rs
quotes: Background removal operator - this should allow removing the input image's background using the `rembg-rs` crate.
Controls set the background removal parameters.

sections.Status: Partial. Implemented with `rembg-rs` on desktop. The web and mobile builds compile a stub that reports an error, and on desktop the user must supply the ONNX model and the ONNX Runtime library ([D-PLAT](findings.md#d-plat)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `BackgroundRemoval::params`: `threshold`, `binary`, `sticker` (the `rembg-rs` `RemovalOptions`) ([bgremove.rs:42-46](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L42)).
- `render` renders the input over its whole extent (`src_req`), calls `compute_mask`, and applies the mask with the `MASK` kernel at any resolution ([bgremove.rs:62](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L62), [bgremove.rs:77-81](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L77), [bgremove.rs:83](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L83), [bgremove.rs:89-97](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L89)).
- `compute_mask` calls `rembg_rs::rembg` with a shared `ModelManager` ([bgremove.rs:101-126](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L101), [bgremove.rs:133-139](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L133)).
- Without the `rembg` feature, `compute_mask` bails ([bgremove.rs:169-172](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L169)); `rembg` is only in the `desktop` feature ([Cargo.toml:8](../../Cargo.toml#L8)).
sections.Tests: None (no model is available to the test suite).
sections.Notes: Extra parameters `invert`, `resolution` and `model` ([bgremove.rs:47-49](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L47)). `render` computes the mask once per input hash and settings, at the chosen `resolution`, and caches it in `engine.cache` ([bgremove.rs:64-77](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L64), [bgremove.rs:84-85](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L84)). `compute_mask` turns a missing ONNX Runtime into an error message (`catch_unwind`) ([bgremove.rs:127-132](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L127)); `resolve_model` searches the parameter, `DELOS_REMBG_MODEL` and `~/.delos/models` ([bgremove.rs:146-167](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L146)). The mask cache key builds on the structural hash, so it inherits the stale-identity defect ([D-STALE](findings.md#d-stale)).

entries.title: Invert
quotes: Invert operator - inverts colors.
No controls.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Invert` has no `params` and its `render` runs `INVERT` ([basic.rs:187-193](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L187)).
- `INVERT` computes `a − c` per channel on premultiplied pixels, which is `a·(1 − C)` for the straight colour `C`: the spec's formula, with alpha kept ([kernels.rs:215-226](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L215)).
sections.Notes: Values are sRGB-encoded, not linear (the `tile.rs` header); the spec does not say which.

entries.title: Clip
quotes: Clip - allows selecting a subset of image.

sections.Implemented by: - `Clip` keeps the rectangle `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` (fractions of the input) ([basic.rs:324-331](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L324)) with an `Overlay::Rect` and is edited on its input (`EditView::Input`) ([basic.rs:337-342](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L337)). `size` rounds to whole pixels ([basic.rs:332-336](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L332)) and `render` maps the request with `input_map` ([basic.rs:343-352](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L343)).

entries.title: Resize with selectable interpolation
quotes: Resize - allows upscaling or downscaling input.
Allows choosing upscale/downscale algorithm to use.
Should offer nearest-neighbor, bilinear, bicubic and fourier-based interpolation.

sections.Status: Partial. All four filters are offered and used when upscaling. When downscaling on both axes, bilinear, bicubic and Fourier all give the same area-averaged result, so the choice only matters between "nearest" and the rest ([D-RESIZE](findings.md#d-resize)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `FILTERS` and `Resize::params` (`scale` and `filter`) ([resize.rs:15](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L15), [resize.rs:55-56](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L55), [resize.rs:58](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L58), [resize.rs:61-63](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L61)).
- `Resize::render`: nearest uses `Sampling::Point` ([resize.rs:88-91](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L88)); coarse grids and size-less inputs return the area-filtered input regardless of filter ([resize.rs:92-98](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L92)); upsampling fetches native pixels and runs `RESAMPLE` with bilinear or bicubic sampling ([resize.rs:99-103](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L99), [resize.rs:107-108](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L107), [resize.rs:119-120](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L119)).
- Fourier: `render` calls `fourier_resample` and resamples its result ([resize.rs:109](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L109), [resize.rs:111-113](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L111), [resize.rs:115-118](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L115)); `fourier_resample` zero-pads or truncates the spectrum, rows then columns ([resize.rs:124-206](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L124)).
- Bicubic is Catmull-Rom (`catmull_rom`) in both backends ([tile.rs:109-120](../../src/engine/tile.rs#L109)).
sections.Notes: Upscaling also falls back to the area path when the native cover exceeds four times the output, with a floor of 65,536 pixels (`native.pixel_count()`), so very large upscales of large regions ignore the filter too ([resize.rs:104-106](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L104)). A `mode` choice between a scale factor and an exact `width`/`height` (`MODES`) is not in the spec ([resize.rs:14](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L14), [resize.rs:57](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L57), [resize.rs:59-60](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L59)).

entries.title: Blend with the Wikipedia blend modes
quotes: Blend operator - allows combining images with the blend modes specified at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blend_modes plus the following:

sections.Status: Implemented. Every mode the article names is present: normal, dissolve, multiply, screen, overlay, hard light, soft light, colour dodge and burn, linear dodge (addition) and burn, divide, subtract, difference, darken only, lighten only, hue, saturation, colour and luminosity. The code adds the modes the article mentions in passing or Photoshop defines (vivid, linear and pin light, hard mix, exclusion), and an `opacity` parameter.
sections.Implemented by:
- `BLEND_MODES` lists `normal` to `linear_burn` ([kernels.rs:341-352](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L341)), `divide`, `subtract`, `difference` ([kernels.rs:357-359](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L357)) and `darken` to `luminosity` ([kernels.rs:361-366](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L361)); `Blend::params` (`mode`) and `render` ([basic.rs:216-218](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L216), [basic.rs:222-228](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L222), [basic.rs:230-231](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L230)).
- Separable modes: `blend_channel` ([kernels.rs:413-423](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L413), [kernels.rs:432-436](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L432), [kernels.rs:438-439](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L438), [kernels.rs:443-445](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L443)); non-separable modes: `blend_color` with `set_lum` and `set_sat` ([kernels.rs:468-493](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L468)); the GPU versions of the same modes are WGSL helpers in `BLEND` (`screen1` to `soft_light`, `blend_channel`, `blend_color` with `set_lum` and `set_sat`) ([kernels.rs:501-521](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L501), [kernels.rs:534-544](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L534), [kernels.rs:555-560](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L555), [kernels.rs:562-563](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L562), [kernels.rs:567](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L567), [kernels.rs:570-599](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L570)); compositing with the backdrop's alpha in `BLEND`'s WGSL `kernel` ([kernels.rs:600-617](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L600)) and `cpu` closure ([kernels.rs:619-646](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L619)).
sections.Notes: Extra modes `vivid_light`, `linear_light`, `pin_light`, `hard_mix` ([kernels.rs:353-356](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L353)) and `exclusion` ([kernels.rs:360](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L360)), computed in `blend_channel` ([kernels.rs:424-431](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L424), [kernels.rs:437](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L437)) with the `vivid_light` helper ([kernels.rs:397-400](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L397)), and in the WGSL ([kernels.rs:522-525](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L522), [kernels.rs:545-554](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L545), [kernels.rs:561](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L561), exclusion is `case 18u`). The `opacity` parameter ([basic.rs:217](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L217), [basic.rs:229](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L229)). Soft light uses the W3C formula (the article lists several). The mode list was checked against the article on 2026-10-14.

entries.title: Logic-gate blend modes
quotes: Logic Gate: applies logic operation (and, or, xor) to both images.
Note that nand, nor and xnor are not included bc they can be achieved with the invert operator.

sections.Implemented by: - `and`, `or` and `xor` are entries 25 to 27 of `BLEND_MODES` ([kernels.rs:367-369](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L367)); `logic` quantises each straight colour channel to 8 bits and applies the operation ([kernels.rs:402-411](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L402)); `blend_channel` dispatches the three modes to it ([kernels.rs:440-442](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L440)), and the WGSL `logic` and `blend_channel` do the same on the GPU ([kernels.rs:526-533](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L526), [kernels.rs:564-566](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L564)).
sections.Notes: The gates apply to colour only; alpha is composited like any other blend mode.

entries.title: Splits produce two complementary outputs
quotes: Splitting an image produces two output images, one for each side of a split border.
One output contains the pixels on one side of the border, with every pixel on the other side transparent.
The other output contains the complementary pixels, with those present in the first output transparent.
This makes localized effects possible, as selections do in a regular editor.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Split` kinds declare two `outputs`; output 0 keeps the `region`, output 1 the rest ([split.rs:21-31](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L21)). `render_output` short-cuts tiles wholly on one side and otherwise runs `SPLIT` with `keep_inside` ([split.rs:110-131](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L110)).
- `SPLIT` keeps the input pixel or returns transparent ([kernels.rs:267-288](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L267)).

entries.title: Vertical, horizontal and rectangle splits and their controls
quotes: Vertical Split (`left` / `right`), Horizontal Split (`top` / `bottom`) and Rectangle Split (`inside` / `outside`) are provided.
Each is controlled in the image view by dragging the border line, or by moving and resizing the rectangle, or via form inputs.

sections.Implemented by:
- `VERTICAL`, `HORIZONTAL` and `RECTANGLE` with their `outputs`, fraction `params` and `overlays` ([split.rs:33-73](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L33)).
- `Overlay::Line` is drawn and dragged (`Drag::Axis`) ([image_view.rs:412-418](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L412), [image_view.rs:427-441](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L427)); `Overlay::Rect` is moved by its body (`RectMove`) and resized by its corners (`RectCorner`) ([image_view.rs:467-470](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L467), [image_view.rs:478-504](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L478)).
sections.Notes: The line overlay shows side labels (`b_text`, `a_text`) ([image_view.rs:420-426](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L420), [image_view.rs:442-444](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L442)); the rectangle overlay shades the outside and shows its size (`shade`, `label`) ([image_view.rs:471-473](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L471), [image_view.rs:477](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L477), [image_view.rs:505](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L505)).

entries.title: Exact partition by pixel centre
quotes: Exact partition: every pixel belongs to exactly one output, decided by its centre.
Stacking the two outputs therefore reproduces the input exactly, at any zoom level.

sections.Implemented by:
- The border is rounded to whole node units in each `region` function ([split.rs:40](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L40), [split.rs:50](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L50), [split.rs:67-72](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L67)).
- `render_output` and `SPLIT` test the pixel centre against the half-open rectangle (`contains`, `inside`) ([split.rs:113-119](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L113), [kernels.rs:274-287](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L274)).

entries.title: Editing view of a split
quotes: Editing view: when a split is selected, the image view shows its whole input with the border controls.

sections.Implemented by: - `Split::edit_view` returns `EditView::Input(0)` ([split.rs:103-106](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L103)), handled by `displayed` (see [F3.2.1](02-editing-and-views.md#f3-2-1)).

entries.title: Specific outputs as inputs, relocation and export targets
quotes: Outputs: the inputs of other nodes, the relocated output and exports can each refer to a specific output of a split.

sections.Status: Partial. The data model supports it everywhere, but "Add node" with a split selected rewires the consumers of its second output onto its first ([D-ADD-AFTER-SPLIT](findings.md#d-add-after-split)).
sections.Implemented by:
- Edges are `Link { node, output }` ([graph.rs:15-27](../../src/graph.rs#L15)); `connect` checks the output exists ([graph.rs:252-254](../../src/graph.rs#L252)).
- The relocated output and export targets are `Link`s: `pinned`, `ExportState::target` ([state.rs:53-54](../../src/ui/state.rs#L53), [state.rs:114-115](../../src/ui/state.rs#L114)).
- The graph view draws one port per output and starts wires from it (`Link::new`) ([graph_view.rs:364-392](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L364)); the inspector's input pickers list every output (`candidates`) ([inspector.rs:75-82](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L75)).
- Structural hashing distinguishes outputs: `link_hash` ([graph.rs:408-416](../../src/graph.rs#L408)).
sections.Notes: The defect: `App::add_node` reconnects all `consumers` of the anchor and feeds the new node output 0 ([state.rs:470-476](../../src/ui/state.rs#L470)).

entries.title: Split sizes
quotes: Size: splits keep their input's size, and splitting a size-less (generative) input splits it at whatever size is requested.

sections.Implemented by: - `Split::size` returns the input size ([split.rs:97-99](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L97)); `region` is computed from `req.extent`, which is the requested extent for size-less inputs ([split.rs:111](../../src/nodes/split.rs#L111)).

entries.title: Any number of outputs per node
quotes: Extensibility: nodes in general may have any number of outputs.
Each node type declares its outputs, and every output of a node has the node's size.

sections.Implemented by:
- `NodeKind::outputs` (default one, "image") and `render_output` ([nodes/mod.rs:204-208](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L204), [nodes/mod.rs:217-222](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L217)).
- One size per node: `Graph::size_of` ("all outputs of a node share it") ([graph.rs:284-287](../../src/graph.rs#L284)).
sections.Notes: Output names in titles and expressions: `link_title` ([graph.rs:151-160](../../src/graph.rs#L151)), `Builder::reference` ([expr.rs:540-555](../../src/expr.rs#L540)). Kernels have at most three inputs (`MAX_INPUTS`); that limits inputs, not outputs.

entries.title: Generators take no inputs
quotes: These operators are differentiated by not taking any inputs.
Rather, they should act as generators of data which can be input to other generators.

sections.Status: Implemented. Generators have no input ports. The second sentence cannot hold literally, since generators take no inputs; the code reads it as "input to other operators" ([D-SPEC-WORDING](findings.md#d-spec-wording)).
sections.Implemented by: - `Generator` does not override `inputs`, so it has none; its category is `Category::Generator` ([generators.rs:21-46](../../src/nodes/generators.rs#L21)).

entries.title: Size-less generators and the output canvas
quotes: Note that generative operators do not have output size - if they are connected directly to output, the user must specify the desired output size (this should be possible to do via WYSIWYG).
As said above, generative operators should generate at the size required of them and should not specify an output size.

sections.Implemented by:
- `NodeKind::size` returns an `Option`, where `None` means size-less ([nodes/mod.rs:212-214](../../src/nodes/mod.rs#L212)); `Generator::size` returns `None` ([generators.rs:37-39](../../src/nodes/generators.rs#L37)); generator kernels normalise coordinates against the requested `extent` (kernel header) ([kernels.rs:649-652](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L649)).
- The output's `canvas_w` and `canvas_h` give the size when its input is size-less: `Output::params` and `Output::size` ([basic.rs:46-51](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L46)), `Graph::canvas` and `extent_of` ([graph.rs:301-308](../../src/graph.rs#L301)).
- WYSIWYG: a corner handle on size-less content (`canvas-handle`) ([image_view.rs:305-322](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L305)) that sets the canvas while dragged (`Drag::Canvas`) ([image_view.rs:277-286](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L277)). Form: the Output node's integer fields.
sections.Tests: `tests/large_images.rs::export_16k_streams_in_bands` (a generator exported at a set canvas).

entries.title: Default canvas fits the window
quotes: The output size which fits naturally into the current Delos window should be selected by default.

sections.Implemented by:
- `fit_canvas_to_window` sets the canvas to 92% of the image viewport unless the user has set it (`canvas_user_set`) ([state.rs:323-344](../../src/ui/state.rs#L323)).
- Called when a generator is added (`add_node`) ([state.rs:484-486](../../src/ui/state.rs#L484)) and whenever size-less content is shown (`sizeless`) ([image_view.rs:69-76](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L69)).
sections.Notes: "Canvas = window size" forces it with `fit_canvas_to_window(true)` ([inspector.rs:199-208](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L199)). The automatic fit writes `canvas_w`/`canvas_h` into the graph without an undo step, and in a project that change is autosaved.

entries.title: Generators adapt to what they are combined with
quotes: If generative operators are connected to combining operators, they will generate at whatever size is necessary to combine successfully with the other side.

sections.Implemented by:
- A combining node's size comes from its definite inputs (`union_size`, `Blend::size`) ([basic.rs:20-24](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L20), [basic.rs:219-221](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L219)).
- `input_request` passes the consumer's `extent` to inputs without a size of their own ([basic.rs:14-18](../../src/nodes/basic.rs#L14)); `size_conflict` ignores size-less inputs (`size_of`) ([graph.rs:352-353](../../src/graph.rs#L352)).
sections.Tests: None checks that a generator adapts to its consumer's size; `tests/project.rs::save_and_load_give_the_same_graph` renders a stack of an image and noise without asserting the size.

entries.title: The initial generators
quotes: The initial generators are: solid color, linear gradient, radial gradient, checkerboard, noise (fBm, turbulence, ridged), Voronoi and Mandelbrot.

sections.Implemented by:
- `SOLID`, `LINEAR`, `RADIAL`, `CHECKER`, `NOISE` (with `NOISE_TYPES` fbm, turbulence, ridged), `VORONOI` and `MANDELBROT` ([generators.rs:61-220](../../src/nodes/generators.rs#L61)).
- Their kernels, `SOLID` to `MANDELBROT` ([kernels.rs:738-976](../../src/engine/kernels.rs#L738)).
sections.Tests: `tests/engine.rs::gpu_matches_cpu` (renders every generator; skipped without a GPU).

entries.title: AI image generation (planned)
quotes: An AI image-generation operator is planned.

sections.Status: Deferred. The spec plans it; nothing implements it.
sections.Implemented by: Nothing. The expensive-result `Cache` used by background removal is the README's intended hook ([cache.rs:12-15](../../src/engine/cache.rs#L12)).

entries.title: Ask which size to use, insert a Resize
quotes: However, the outputs produced by imported images and by combining operators will have a definite size.
In this case, Delos should ask which output size must be used and insert a resizing node after one of the inputs as appropriate.

sections.Status: Implemented. A third answer, "Keep both sizes (align top-left)", is not in the spec.
sections.Implemented by:
- `Graph::size_conflict` finds two definite input sizes that differ on a node with `combines_inputs` ([graph.rs:347-363](../../src/graph.rs#L347)).
- `after_edit` looks for a conflict after every edit ([state.rs:304-313](../../src/ui/state.rs#L304)).
- `ConflictDialog` asks and calls `insert_resize` on the other input ([dialogs.rs:11-57](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L11)); `insert_resize` adds a `Resize` set by `resize_to` ([graph.rs:367-375](../../src/graph.rs#L367)).
sections.Notes: The third answer calls `ignore_conflict` ([dialogs.rs:58](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L58), [state.rs:315-319](../../src/ui/state.rs#L315)), and `after_edit` then skips ignored conflicts. The two resize buttons call `edit`, whose `after_edit` records the next conflict, and then `conflict.set(None)` erases it ([dialogs.rs:42-55](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L42)). A second conflict elsewhere in the graph is therefore not shown until the next edit ([D-CONFLICT](findings.md#d-conflict)).

entries.title: Two ways of working; quick mode
quotes: Delos supports two ways of working:
Quick mode is for one-off edits and quick work.
Imported images are used where they are and nothing is saved.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Session` is `Fresh`, `Quick` or `Project` ([session.rs:14-24](../../src/ui/session.rs#L14)).
- In quick mode, `start_imports` sets `keep_bytes` to false, so nothing is copied ([session.rs:277](../../src/ui/session.rs#L277)); `Worker::import` decodes the image from its path or bytes and keeps that path as its `origin` ([worker.rs:250-256](../../src/worker.rs#L250), [worker.rs:266-269](../../src/worker.rs#L266)).
- `use_autosave` saves only a `Session::Project` ([session.rs:255](../../src/ui/session.rs#L255), [session.rs:263-265](../../src/ui/session.rs#L263)).

entries.title: Project mode
quotes: Project mode is for longer-term work, and for sharing and collaborating with others.

sections.Status: Implemented, as far as a purpose statement can be: projects persist, reopen and can be shared as archives. There is no collaboration beyond exchanging archives (no merging, no concurrent editing); the spec does not ask for more.
sections.Implemented by: - `Project` is a directory ([project.rs:33-36](../../src/project.rs#L33)); see [P8](#p8) to [P15](#p15).

entries.title: First import asks whether to start a project
quotes: When the user imports an image and neither a project nor a quick-mode session is open, Delos asks whether to create a project.

sections.Status: Implemented on desktop and mobile. On the web, where projects are not supported, the first import starts quick mode without asking (as [X2](#x2) expects).
sections.Implemented by:
- `session::import` opens a `ProjectPrompt` holding the pending imports when the session is `Fresh` and `PROJECTS_SUPPORTED` ([session.rs:105-115](../../src/ui/session.rs#L105)); `PROJECTS_SUPPORTED` is the `native` feature ([session.rs:86-87](../../src/ui/session.rs#L86)).
- `ProjectDialog` titles it "Start a project?" when imports are pending (`from_import`) and offers "Quick mode" and "Create project" ([dialogs.rs:210](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L210), [dialogs.rs:221](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L221), [dialogs.rs:281-288](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L281), [dialogs.rs:292-302](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L292)).
sections.Notes: Cancelling the prompt (× or Escape) drops the pending imports and stays `Fresh`.

entries.title: The question mentions the storage cost
quotes: The question makes clear that projects copy every imported image, so they take more storage.

sections.Implemented by: - The dialog text: every image is `copied` into `inputs/`, "so projects take more disk space than the original files" ([dialogs.rs:231-238](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L231)).

entries.title: Declining starts quick mode for good
quotes: If the user declines, a quick-mode session starts and later imports are added to it without asking again.

sections.Implemented by: - `choose_quick` sets `Session::Quick` and runs the pending imports ([session.rs:123-131](../../src/ui/session.rs#L123)); `import` asks only while `Fresh` and otherwise goes straight to `start_imports` ([session.rs:105](../../src/ui/session.rs#L105), [session.rs:119](../../src/ui/session.rs#L119)).

entries.title: Accepting creates a named project in the default location
quotes: If the user accepts, a project is created (named by the user; by default in `~/.delos/projects/<name>`, overridable with `DELOS_PROJECTS_DIR`) and the image is added to it.

sections.Implemented by:
- `default_root` reads `DELOS_PROJECTS_DIR`, else `~/.delos/projects` ([project.rs:38-45](../../src/project.rs#L38)); the prompt's name defaults to the image's file `stem` and its folder to `projects_root` ([session.rs:107-112](../../src/ui/session.rs#L107)); the user edits the name through `set_prompt_name` ([session.rs:140-143](../../src/ui/session.rs#L140)).
- `create_project` joins the name to the chosen folder and asks `Worker::create_project` to run `Project::create`, which makes the folder ([session.rs:156](../../src/ui/session.rs#L156), [session.rs:164](../../src/ui/session.rs#L164), [worker.rs:326-333](../../src/worker.rs#L326), [project.rs:73-76](../../src/project.rs#L73)).
- `pump` hands `Msg::ProjectCreated` to `on_project_created` ([mod.rs:221](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L221)), which switches to `Session::Project` and starts the pending imports (`start_imports`, which sets `keep_bytes` in a project) ([session.rs:172](../../src/ui/session.rs#L172), [session.rs:174](../../src/ui/session.rs#L174), [session.rs:177-179](../../src/ui/session.rs#L177)); the next autosave copies the image into `inputs/` (`sync_inputs`, see [P9](#p9)).
sections.Notes: The name is passed through `sanitize_name` to make a folder name; the location can be changed with a folder picker on desktop. `create_project` refuses an existing non-empty folder with a message in the dialog ([session.rs:157-162](../../src/ui/session.rs#L157)), and `Project::create` checks the same ([project.rs:70-72](../../src/project.rs#L70)).

entries.title: New project from current work
quotes: The current work can also be turned into a project at any time ("New project from current work").
The images the graph uses are copied into it.

sections.Implemented by:
- The Project menu item, labelled "Save as new project…" when a project is already open ([mod.rs:525-533](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L525)), opens the prompt with no pending imports (`prompt_new_project`) ([session.rs:134-137](../../src/ui/session.rs#L134)).
- After `on_project_created` switches the session, `use_autosave` saves the current graph, and `sync_inputs` copies every image it uses ([session.rs:255](../../src/ui/session.rs#L255), [session.rs:263-265](../../src/ui/session.rs#L263), [project.rs:141-153](../../src/project.rs#L141)).

entries.title: The footer shows mode, location and save state
quotes: The bottom of the window always shows whether Delos is in quick mode or in a project (with its name and location), and whether the project's changes are saved.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Footer` reads the `session` and `save_state` ([mod.rs:560-561](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L560)) and shows "No project", "Quick mode" or "Project" with `name` and `dir`, and the `SaveState` as "Saving…", "All changes saved" or "Not saved: …" ([mod.rs:563-575](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L563), [mod.rs:578-579](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L578), [mod.rs:584-586](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L584)).
- `Worker::save_project` reports each save as `Msg::ProjectSaved` ([worker.rs:376](../../src/worker.rs#L376)), which sets the state ([mod.rs:225-231](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L225)).
sections.Notes: The desktop window title also shows the mode (`set_title`). The invariants model notes that out-of-order save completions could show "All changes saved" early (its fragile spot 10).

entries.title: Autosave after every change
quotes: Projects are saved automatically after every change.

sections.Implemented by:
- `use_autosave` is an effect on `graph` and `session`: each change bumps `seq` and calls `Worker::save_project` with every image the session holds (`all_images`) ([session.rs:251-256](../../src/ui/session.rs#L251), [session.rs:263-265](../../src/ui/session.rs#L263)).
- `save_project` runs in the background (`run_background`), serialises the graph with `to_text` and writes `project.delos` with `save_text` ([worker.rs:356](../../src/worker.rs#L356), [worker.rs:360](../../src/worker.rs#L360), [worker.rs:365](../../src/worker.rs#L365), [worker.rs:367-373](../../src/worker.rs#L367)).
sections.Notes: "Every change" includes moving nodes in the graph view (positions are saved as `:at`) and the automatic canvas fit ([N3](03-operators.md#n3)). `save_project` skips saves older than the last written one (`saved_seq`) ([worker.rs:361-364](../../src/worker.rs#L361)), syncs `inputs/` first (`sync_inputs`, see [P10](#p10)) ([worker.rs:366](../../src/worker.rs#L366)), and rewrites `project.delos` only when its text changed ([worker.rs:368](../../src/worker.rs#L368)).

entries.title: Atomic saves
quotes: Saves are atomic, so a project file is never left half-written.

sections.Status: Implemented, without `fsync`: a crash cannot leave a half-written file in place, but power loss can lose the last save.
sections.Implemented by:
- `write_atomic` writes a temporary file and renames it ([project.rs:390-399](../../src/project.rs#L390)); `save_text` uses it for `project.delos` ([project.rs:191-193](../../src/project.rs#L191)) and `add_input` for copied images ([project.rs:103](../../src/project.rs#L103)).
- `share` writes the archive the same way (`tmp_path`, then `rename`) ([project.rs:258](../../src/project.rs#L258), [project.rs:277-283](../../src/project.rs#L277)).
sections.Tests: None (atomicity under failure is not tested).

entries.title: Opening a project writes nothing
quotes: Opening a project does not change anything on disk until the user edits it.

sections.Status: Partial. The autosave skips the first run after opening, but a generator-only project can be rewritten without any edit: `replace_document` resets `canvas_user_set`, and the image view's automatic canvas fit then writes `canvas_w`/`canvas_h` when the window size differs, which autosaves ([D-OPEN-WRITES](findings.md#d-open-writes)).
sections.Implemented by: - `on_project_opened` sets `SaveState::Saved` ([session.rs:210-211](../../src/ui/session.rs#L210)); `use_autosave` skips the first run after the project directory changes while the state is `Saved` (`switched`) ([session.rs:257-262](../../src/ui/session.rs#L257)).
sections.Tests: `tests/project_e2e.rs::opening_a_project_does_not_rewrite_it` (runs headless, with no viewport, so the canvas fit never fires).
sections.Notes: The fit: `fit_canvas_to_window` ([state.rs:323-344](../../src/ui/state.rs#L323)), called by the image view whenever size-less content is shown ([image_view.rs:69-76](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L69)); `canvas_user_set` is reset in `replace_document` ([state.rs:257](../../src/ui/state.rs#L257)). Confirmed by a failing probe ([D-OPEN-WRITES](findings.md#d-open-writes)). Importing a `.delosproject` necessarily writes the unpacked copy; the clause concerns the opened project's own files.

entries.title: Confirm before leaving quick mode with work
quotes: Leaving a quick-mode session that has work in it asks for confirmation.

sections.Status: Partial. On desktop, End quick session and opening a project ask first. On mobile, `confirm` answers yes without asking. On the web the Project menu is hidden, so the only way to leave is closing the tab, and on every platform closing the window or quitting is not intercepted ([D-QUICK-EXIT](findings.md#d-quick-exit)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `has_unsaved_work`: not `Fresh`, not a project, more than the output node ([session.rs:243-245](../../src/ui/session.rs#L243)).
- Callers: "End quick session" (`close`) ([mod.rs:509-517](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L509)), opening a project from the menu (`open_with`) ([mod.rs:479-481](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L479)) or by dropping one, also guarded by `has_unsaved_work` ([mod.rs:96](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L96)).
- `platform::confirm` shows a native dialog on desktop and returns `true` elsewhere ([platform.rs:217-236](../../src/ui/platform.rs#L217)).
sections.Tests: `tests/project_e2e.rs::quick_mode_imports_without_copying` asserts `has_unsaved_work`; the confirmation itself is UI and untested.

entries.title: A project is a directory with project.delos and inputs/
quotes: A project is a directory:

sections.Implemented by:
- `PROJECT_FILE` and `INPUTS_DIR` ([project.rs:29-30](../../src/project.rs#L29)); `Project::create` makes `inputs/` and writes an empty graph ([project.rs:73-76](../../src/project.rs#L73)).
- Images are referred to as `inputs/<file>` (`add_input`) ([project.rs:112](../../src/project.rs#L112)).

entries.title: Images copied unchanged, or as PNG
quotes: Imported images are copied into `inputs/` unchanged (no re-encoding) when their original bytes are available.
Images known only by their pixels are written as PNG.

sections.Implemented by:
- `adopt_image` copies the bytes of the image's `origin` file, else encodes `to_rgba8` as PNG, and points the image at its copy (`set_project_file`) ([project.rs:117-131](../../src/project.rs#L117)). `add_input` writes those bytes as they are into `inputs/` (`write_atomic`) ([project.rs:90-93](../../src/project.rs#L90), [project.rs:101-104](../../src/project.rs#L101)).
- Images dropped or picked without a path keep their bytes in the session stash when a project is open (`keep_bytes`), so they too have an `origin` ([worker.rs:257-264](../../src/worker.rs#L257)).
sections.Notes: `add_input` reuses an identical file of the same name and otherwise picks a free name ([project.rs:98-111](../../src/project.rs#L98)).

entries.title: inputs/ holds exactly the images in use
quotes: `inputs/` contains exactly the images the current graph uses.
Images that are no longer used are removed from it.

sections.Implemented by: - `sync_inputs` adopts used images that lack a file and moves every other file out to the stash ([project.rs:142-153](../../src/project.rs#L142), [project.rs:154-175](../../src/project.rs#L154)); it runs before each save ([worker.rs:366](../../src/worker.rs#L366)).
sections.Notes: Hidden files, `*.tmp` files and anything that is not a regular file (subfolders) are left alone. Until the first edit after opening, a stray file in `inputs/` stays (by [P6.2](#p6-2)).

entries.title: Undo history is not part of the project
quotes: Undo history is not part of a project.
It belongs to the editing session and is not expected to survive closing and reopening a project.

sections.Implemented by:
- `History` (undo and redo stacks of `Graph` snapshots) lives in `App`, not in the project ([state.rs:100-106](../../src/ui/state.rs#L100)); `replace_document` clears it on open and close ([state.rs:249](../../src/ui/state.rs#L249)).
- `to_text` serialises only the graph ([expr.rs:376](../../src/expr.rs#L376)).

entries.title: Images the history needs live in a session stash
quotes: Within a session, images the history may still need are kept outside the project (in a temporary session folder).

sections.Implemented by:
- `new_stash_dir` makes a per-session folder under the system temp directory, named from the process id and `now_ms` ([worker.rs:402-403](../../src/worker.rs#L402), [worker.rs:413-414](../../src/worker.rs#L413)).
- `sync_inputs` moves unused files there and repoints every `known` image to the stashed copy (`set_origin`) ([project.rs:163-180](../../src/project.rs#L163)).
sections.Notes: The decoded pixels of every image in the history also stay in memory (up to `HISTORY_LIMIT` = 60 snapshots). `new_stash_dir` also prunes stashes left by earlier sessions that are older than a day ([worker.rs:404-412](../../src/worker.rs#L404)).

entries.title: Undo copies images back unchanged
quotes: If an undo brings an image back, it is copied back into `inputs/` unchanged.

sections.Implemented by: - After an undo, the next autosave's `sync_inputs` finds the image without a project file and calls `adopt_image`, which copies the stashed bytes (`origin`) ([project.rs:148-153](../../src/project.rs#L148), [project.rs:118-120](../../src/project.rs#L118)).
sections.Notes: If the stash was pruned (another instance, a session longer than a day), the image is re-encoded as PNG instead: the pixels survive, the bytes do not.

entries.title: Share Project writes a .delosproject zip
quotes: Share Project exports the current project as a `.delosproject` file: a zip archive containing the project directory.

sections.Status: Implemented on desktop. On mobile the menu item is hidden (no pickers, [X1](#x1)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `Project::share` zips the directory under one top-level folder ([project.rs:260-268](../../src/project.rs#L260), [project.rs:271-274](../../src/project.rs#L271)).
- The menu item's `share` handler asks for a destination (`pick_save_path`) and calls `share_project` ([mod.rs:491-500](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L491)).
sections.Notes: `share` deflates `project.delos` and stores images as they are (`CompressionMethod`) ([project.rs:269-270](../../src/project.rs#L269)). `Worker::share_project` holds the save lock while packing, so the archive matches a finished save ([worker.rs:385-386](../../src/worker.rs#L385)).

entries.title: Import Project accepts three forms
quotes: Import Project accepts a `.delosproject` file, a `project.delos` file or a project directory.

sections.Status: Implemented. The menu splits it in two: "Import project…" for files and "Open project folder…" for directories.
sections.Implemented by:
- `project::open` dispatches on `ARCHIVE_EXT`, `PROJECT_FILE` or a directory ([project.rs:290-298](../../src/project.rs#L290)).
- Menu items `import_file` and `import_folder` ([mod.rs:535-536](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L535)), built with `open_with`, which runs a picker (`pick_project_file` or `pick_folder`) and then `open_project` ([mod.rs:472-478](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L472), [mod.rs:482](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L482), [mod.rs:487](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L487), [mod.rs:489](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L489), [platform.rs:172-173](../../src/ui/platform.rs#L172), [platform.rs:183](../../src/ui/platform.rs#L183)).
- `on_project_opened` replaces the document with the loaded graph and switches to `Session::Project` ([mod.rs:223](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L223), [session.rs:205-209](../../src/ui/session.rs#L205)).
sections.Notes: The file picker accepts any `*.delos` file (`pick_project_file`), but `open` accepts only one named exactly `project.delos`, so `other.delos` passes the picker and is then refused.

entries.title: Archives unpack under a new name
quotes: A `.delosproject` file is unpacked into the projects folder under a new name, so it never overwrites an existing project.

sections.Implemented by: - `unpack` opens the archive, finds the project inside it (at the root or in one top folder) and names the copy after that folder or the archive's `stem` ([project.rs:306-307](../../src/project.rs#L306), [project.rs:317-327](../../src/project.rs#L317)), then extracts every entry into `unique_dir(root, name)` ([project.rs:328-355](../../src/project.rs#L328)); `unique_dir` appends `-2`, `-3`… ([project.rs:54-64](../../src/project.rs#L54)). `root` is the projects folder (`projects_root`) ([session.rs:197-198](../../src/ui/session.rs#L197)).

entries.title: Directories open in place
quotes: A directory is opened in place, without copying.

sections.Implemented by: - `open` builds a `Project` with the directory itself as `dir` ([project.rs:294-295](../../src/project.rs#L294)).

entries.title: Opening by drag and drop
quotes: Projects can also be opened by dropping them onto the window.

sections.Status: Implemented on desktop only (the drop path needs the file's path, a `desktop` feature).
sections.Implemented by: - `Root`'s drop handler finds the first dropped item that `is_project_path` and passes it to `open_project` ([mod.rs:92-99](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L92), [mod.rs:244-249](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L244)).

entries.title: Verify the structure before opening
quotes: Before opening, Delos verifies the structure:
`project.delos` exists and parses;
`inputs/` exists;
every image the graph refers to exists inside `inputs/`.
It reports precisely what is wrong otherwise.

sections.Implemented by:
