- `Project::verify` checks the file, the folder, the parse and each `image_files` path, with a message naming the project, the line and the image ([project.rs:206-225](../../src/project.rs#L206)). `load` calls it first and `unpack` calls it after extracting ([project.rs:231](../../src/project.rs#L231), [project.rs:357](../../src/project.rs#L357)).
- Failures reach the user as a toast (`on_project_opened`) ([session.rs:214](../../src/ui/session.rs#L214)).
sections.Notes: Missing-image messages give a line but no column (see [E11](05-expressions.md#e11)). `inputs/` is checked before parsing, the reverse of the spec's order; the outcome is the same.

entries.title: Unsafe paths are rejected; failed imports leave nothing
quotes: Paths that would point outside the project, whether in the project file or inside an archive, are rejected.
A failed import leaves nothing behind.

sections.Status: Partial. Unsafe paths are rejected. A failed import leaves nothing behind only when the failure is in extraction or `verify`: if the unpacked project then fails to *load* (an image that does not decode, an unknown node kind), `open` returns the error and the unpacked folder stays in the projects folder ([D-IMPORT-LEFTOVER](findings.md#d-import-leftover)).
sections.Implemented by:
- In the project file: `resolve` accepts only `inputs/` followed by normal components ([project.rs:195-204](../../src/project.rs#L195)).
- In an archive: `unpack` checks every entry before extracting and refuses one without an `enclosed_name` ([project.rs:310-316](../../src/project.rs#L310)).
- Cleanup: `unpack` extracts and verifies inside one fallible `result` and removes the destination when extraction or `verify` fails ([project.rs:330](../../src/project.rs#L330), [project.rs:356-363](../../src/project.rs#L356)); an archive without `project.delos` is refused before anything is created ([project.rs:323](../../src/project.rs#L323)).
sections.Notes: The defect: `open` calls `load` after `unpack` returns, with no cleanup ([project.rs:291](../../src/project.rs#L291), [project.rs:299](../../src/project.rs#L299)). Confirmed by a failing probe ([D-IMPORT-LEFTOVER](findings.md#d-import-leftover)).

entries.title: Mobile: projects without pickers
quotes: Projects are currently desktop-first:
Mobile supports projects but has no file pickers yet, so Import and Share Project are unavailable there.

sections.Implemented by: - `mobile` enables `native`, hence projects ([Cargo.toml:9](../../Cargo.toml#L9)); `HAS_PICKERS` is the `desktop` feature ([platform.rs:164-165](../../src/ui/platform.rs#L164)) and hides Import, Open folder and Share ([mod.rs:534-544](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L534)).
sections.Notes: On mobile, exports go to `~/Documents` without asking (`choose_save_target`) ([platform.rs:129-135](../../src/ui/platform.rs#L129)).

entries.title: Web: always quick mode
quotes: Web has no file system and always works in quick mode.

sections.Implemented by: - `web` does not enable `native` ([Cargo.toml:10-11](../../Cargo.toml#L10)), so `PROJECTS_SUPPORTED` is false ([session.rs:86-87](../../src/ui/session.rs#L86)): the Project menu is hidden ([mod.rs:384-386](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L384)) and the first import starts `Session::Quick` ([session.rs:106](../../src/ui/session.rs#L106), [session.rs:117](../../src/ui/session.rs#L117)).

entries.title: Platform limits accepted for now
quotes: These limitations are accepted for now.
Full functionality on all platforms is a later goal.

sections.Implemented by: Nothing; the README lists the same gaps.
sections.Notes: The accepted limits are the project ones. The other platform gaps found here ([D-PLAT](findings.md#d-plat)) are not covered by this acceptance.

entries.title: A Lisp-like plain-text form of the graph
quotes: The node graph has a plain-text representation, so we can speak of Delos *expressions*.
It is a Lisp-like format, in keeping with layer stacks being treated as non-empty lists:

sections.Implemented by:
- `parse` reads top-level forms into `Sexp` lists, symbols, strings and numbers ([expr.rs:101-112](../../src/expr.rs#L101)); `Parser::form` ([expr.rs:152-202](../../src/expr.rs#L152)).
- `to_text` prints a graph, and `build`/`from_text` read one ([expr.rs:382-442](../../src/expr.rs#L382), [expr.rs:470-511](../../src/expr.rs#L470)). `Project::save` uses `to_text`, and `Project::load` parses through `verify` and calls `expr::build` ([project.rs:186-189](../../src/project.rs#L186), [project.rs:231](../../src/project.rs#L231), [project.rs:250](../../src/project.rs#L250)).
sections.Notes: The spec's example uses `def` for a node used twice; `to_text` binds a node with `def` when it has two or more consumers or several outputs (`shared`) ([expr.rs:408-426](../../src/expr.rs#L408)).

entries.title: Nodes, inputs in port order, `_` for empty ports
quotes: A node is written `(kind input… :param value…)`.
Inputs come in port order, and `_` leaves a port empty.

sections.Implemented by:
- Printing: `Printer::node` writes the inputs up to the last connected one, with `_` for empty ports (`reference`) ([expr.rs:352-353](../../src/expr.rs#L352), [expr.rs:317](../../src/expr.rs#L317)).
- Reading: `Builder::fill` separates `:key value` pairs from `positional` inputs, checks the `ports` count and connects each input ([expr.rs:584-602](../../src/expr.rs#L584), [expr.rs:628-637](../../src/expr.rs#L628)); `Builder::input` maps `_` to an empty port ([expr.rs:526](../../src/expr.rs#L526)).

entries.title: Several outputs: `def` and `name.output`
quotes: Nodes with several outputs (splits) are always bound with `def`, and each output is referred to as `name.output`, e.g. `s.left`.

sections.Status: Implemented. One exception the spec does not mention: a split with no consumers is written as a plain detached form, without `def`, since nothing refers to its outputs.
sections.Implemented by:
- Printing: nodes with several `outputs` are in `shared` even with one consumer ([expr.rs:408-411](../../src/expr.rs#L408)); `Printer::reference` writes `name.output` ([expr.rs:320-322](../../src/expr.rs#L320)).
- Reading: `Builder::input` passes names to `Builder::reference` ([expr.rs:527](../../src/expr.rs#L527)), which resolves `name.output` and explains the alternatives when it is missing or wrong ([expr.rs:540-555](../../src/expr.rs#L540)); `Builder::input` rejects an inline multi-output node ([expr.rs:531-533](../../src/expr.rs#L531)).

entries.title: `(stack front … back)`
quotes: `(stack front … back)` is a layer stack.

sections.Implemented by:
- Printing: a chain of single-use, untitled stacks (`collapsed`) is flattened into one list ([expr.rs:336-348](../../src/expr.rs#L336), [expr.rs:389](../../src/expr.rs#L389)).
- Reading: `fill` builds the chain with `set_stack_layers` when there are more than two layers ([expr.rs:618-627](../../src/expr.rs#L618)).
sections.Notes: A stack in the middle of a chain that has its own title is printed as a nested `(stack …)` so the title survives.

entries.title: `(image "inputs/…")`
quotes: `(image "inputs/…")` is a static image.

sections.Implemented by:
- Printing: the node's project path from `image_file` ([expr.rs:349-350](../../src/expr.rs#L349), [expr.rs:38-41](../../src/expr.rs#L38)); `to_text` refuses images without a project file ([expr.rs:376-381](../../src/expr.rs#L376)).
- Reading: `fill` asks the caller's `image` function for the decoded image and sets the derived parameters ([expr.rs:603-614](../../src/expr.rs#L603)).
sections.Notes: `fill` also gives the node a default `label`, the file name ([expr.rs:615](../../src/expr.rs#L615)). `image_files` lists the paths so a project can be verified before it is built ([expr.rs:448-466](../../src/expr.rs#L448)).

entries.title: `:at` and `:title`
quotes: `:at (x y)` is a node's position in the graph view, and `:title "…"` gives it a custom title.

sections.Implemented by:
- Printing: `:title` unless it is an image's implicit file-name title, and always `:at` ([expr.rs:364-370](../../src/expr.rs#L364)).
- Reading: `Builder::attribute` handles `at` and `title` ([expr.rs:644-653](../../src/expr.rs#L644)).

entries.title: Values and comments
quotes: Values are numbers, `true`/`false`, choices as symbols, colors as `(r g b a)` lists and text as strings.
Comments start with `;`.

sections.Implemented by:
- Printing: `value_text` ([expr.rs:293-302](../../src/expr.rs#L293)).
- Reading: `parse_value` checks each value against the parameter's default type and choice list ([expr.rs:698-745](../../src/expr.rs#L698)); `skip_space` drops `;` comments ([expr.rs:141-144](../../src/expr.rs#L141)).
sections.Notes: Colours may also be written `(r g b)`; alpha then defaults to 1.

entries.title: Write every parameter; read with defaults and auto-layout
quotes: When saving, every parameter is written, including defaults, so a project keeps its meaning if a default changes later.
When reading, omitted parameters take their defaults, and nodes without `:at` are laid out automatically, so expressions can be written by hand.

sections.Status: Implemented, with one deliberate exception: a static image's derived parameters (image id, width, height) are not written, because they come from the file (`IMAGE_DERIVED`).
sections.Implemented by:
- Printing: `Printer::node` writes every `ParamDef`, falling back to its default ([expr.rs:355-363](../../src/expr.rs#L355)); `IMAGE_DERIVED` ([expr.rs:35-36](../../src/expr.rs#L35)).
- Reading: nodes start from `default_params` (`add_node_at`) ([graph.rs:136](../../src/graph.rs#L136)); `Builder::layout` places nodes without `:at` in columns by depth ([expr.rs:667-695](../../src/expr.rs#L667)).

entries.title: Fast serialisation
quotes: Serializing and deserializing must be fast.

sections.Implemented by:
- `Doc::width` stops measuring once a list cannot fit, keeping pretty-printing linear ([expr.rs:221-237](../../src/expr.rs#L221)).
- `Project::load` decodes images in parallel before building (`into_par_iter`) ([project.rs:235-248](../../src/project.rs#L235)).
sections.Notes: "Fast" has no number in the spec. The README reports 5 ms to serialise and 16 ms to load a 3,400-node graph.

entries.title: Round trip gives a functionally identical graph
quotes: Doing both must give a functionally identical graph: the same nodes, connections, parameters, titles and positions, rendering the same pixels.

sections.Implemented by:
- The printer and builder above; node ids are renumbered on load, which "functionally identical" allows.
- Positions are rounded to whole units when printed (`:at`) ([expr.rs:370](../../src/expr.rs#L370)).
sections.Notes: Floating-point parameters print with Rust's shortest round-trip form, so they read back bit for bit (the value test checks `0.3333333333333333`).

entries.title: Errors with line and column
quotes: Errors are reported with a line and column.

sections.Status: Partial. Syntax and semantic errors of the expression carry a line and a column. When a project is verified, a missing or unsafe image path is reported with its line only ([D-ERROR-COLUMN](findings.md#d-error-column)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `ExprError` with `line` and `col`, displayed as `line L:C: message` ([expr.rs:48-65](../../src/expr.rs#L48)); every `Sexp` keeps its `Pos` ([expr.rs:70-90](../../src/expr.rs#L70)).
- `Project::verify` formats only `pos.line` for image errors ([project.rs:218-223](../../src/project.rs#L218)).

entries.title: Regression tests for fixed bugs
quotes: Bugs that are fixed must get regression tests that reproduce them.

sections.Status: Process. Regression tests exist for the UI-state bugs fixed so far. Whether every fixed bug got one cannot be read from the code. The two open defects found by the invariants model have probes but no tests in `tests/`, which is consistent with the rule since they are not fixed.
sections.Implemented by: - The headless UI harness `with_app` runs scenarios against a real `App` ([ui_state.rs:34-41](../../tests/ui_state.rs#L34)).
sections.Notes: Checking this clause properly needs the bug history (commit messages or an issue tracker) next to the tests; `spectrace impact` on a fix commit lists the entries it touches, which is where its regression test should appear.

entries.title: Projects: unit and end-to-end tests on the real services
quotes: Project features must be covered by unit tests and by end-to-end tests.
The end-to-end tests run the application's real state, background worker and autosave without a window, and drive them as the user interface does.

sections.Status: Process. Both suites exist. Every project clause in [04-sessions-and-projects.md](04-sessions-and-projects.md) except [P3.1](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p3-1), [P6.1](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p6-1), [P7](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p7), [P13.3](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p13-3), [X1](04-sessions-and-projects.md#x1) and [X2](04-sessions-and-projects.md#x2) cites at least one test.
sections.Implemented by:
- `use_services` builds the same `App`, `Worker`, message `pump` and `use_autosave` for the window and for tests ([mod.rs:44-46](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L44), [mod.rs:49-54](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L49)); session actions are plain functions of `App` so tests call what buttons call (`session.rs` header) ([session.rs:4-6](../../src/ui/session.rs#L4)).
- The harness `Delos::start` runs a headless `VirtualDom` and drives it with `run` and `until` ([project_e2e.rs:39-77](../../tests/project_e2e.rs#L39)).
sections.Tests: `tests/project.rs::create_makes_the_project_layout` (and the rest of `tests/project.rs`), `tests/project_e2e.rs::first_import_asks_and_creates_a_project` (and the rest of `tests/project_e2e.rs`).

entries.title: 16K performance tests
quotes: Performance at 16K resolution is tested: previews must stay interactive, and exports must run in bounded memory.

sections.Status: Process. The tests exist and assert time budgets on both backends. Bounded export memory is asserted only for the band size of a generator export, and only PNG is exported at 16K; the formats that buffer the whole image are not tested ([D-EXPORT-MEMORY](findings.md#d-export-memory)).
sections.Implemented by:
- `build_graph` makes a 16384² image through invert, reflect, an overlay blend with noise and a stack with a gradient ([large_images.rs:60-69](../../tests/large_images.rs#L60), [large_images.rs:82-102](../../tests/large_images.rs#L82)).
- Previews of 1080² and 1920×1080 must take under 400 ms each (`budget`) ([large_images.rs:106-140](../../tests/large_images.rs#L106)); the band `peak` is asserted in `export_16k_streams_in_bands` ([large_images.rs:183-195](../../tests/large_images.rs#L183)).
sections.Notes: `export_16k_png` is ignored in debug builds; run the suite with `--release`.

entries.title: Add node after a split rewires the second output
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Kind: Defect. Confirmed by the probe `add_node_after_a_split_keeps_each_consumer_on_its_output` of the invariants model (its finding 2).
sections.Clauses: [S5](03-operators.md#s5): "the inputs of other nodes … can each refer to a specific output of a split".
sections.Observed: With a split selected, "Add node" moves *every* `consumers` of the split, from both outputs, onto the new node, and feeds the new node the split's output 0 ([state.rs:470-476](../../src/ui/state.rs#L470)). A node that read `split.right` now reads an effect applied to `split.left`.
sections.Consequence: The localised-effect pattern the spec motivates splits with (split, effect on one side, stack) quietly breaks: both layers show the same half. Undo restores it.
sections.Decision: Which output should "Add node after this split" attach to: output 0, the output being viewed, or one the user picks? Or should it be refused for nodes with several outputs? A regression test should come with the fix ([Q1](06-quality.md#q1)).

entries.title: Stale image after undo or a new document
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Kind: Defect. Confirmed by the probe `structural_hash_distinguishes_images_after_undo` of the invariants model (its finding 1).
sections.Clauses: [F2.1](02-editing-and-views.md#f2-1) (the view shows what goes to the output), [O5](03-operators.md#o5) (background removal).
sections.Observed: A static image is identified in the structural hash by a graph-local id from `fresh_id` ([graph.rs:109-113](../../src/graph.rs#L109)); undo and `Graph::new` reuse ids. The preview `key` is that hash ([image_view.rs:107-120](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L107)), and the background-removal mask cache key builds on it (`link_hash`) ([bgremove.rs:66-70](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L66)).
sections.Consequence, derived from the code: Import A, undo, import B of the same size: no render is requested and the view keeps showing A. A background-removal node then masks B with A's cutout until the cache entry is evicted.
sections.Decision: None about the spec, which is clear; this is a fix. The invariants model proposes hashing the process-unique `SourceImage::id` instead.

entries.title: A failed project import can leave a folder behind
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Kind: Defect. Found by the independent review. **Confirmed.** Probe `failed_import_leaves_nothing_behind` ([probes/spec_probes.rs](probes/spec_probes.rs)): the import fails and leaves `future/` in the projects folder.
sections.Observed: `unpack` deletes the destination only when extraction or `verify` fails ([project.rs:360-362](../../src/project.rs#L360)). `open` then calls `load`, which decodes the images and builds the graph, and returns its error without cleaning up ([project.rs:289-301](../../src/project.rs#L289)). An archive with a well-formed structure but an image that does not decode, or a node kind this version does not know, fails to open and leaves its unpacked copy in the projects folder.
sections.Decision: None about the spec; this is a fix (move the `load` inside `unpack`'s cleanup, or clean up in `open`). A regression test should build such an archive, as `import_rejects_invalid_archives_and_cleans_up` does for invalid ones.

entries.title: Opening a generator-only project can rewrite it
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Kind: Defect. Found by the independent review. **Confirmed.** Probe `opening_a_generator_project_writes_nothing` ([probes/spec_probes.rs](probes/spec_probes.rs)): after opening, with a 1000×800 image pane, `project.delos` is rewritten with `:canvas_w 920 :canvas_h 736`.
sections.Clauses: [P6.2](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p6-2): "Opening a project does not change anything on disk until the user edits it."
sections.Observed: `replace_document` resets `canvas_user_set` ([state.rs:257](../../src/ui/state.rs#L257)). When the shown content is size-less, the image view calls `fit_canvas_to_window(false)` ([image_view.rs:69-76](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L69)), which writes `canvas_w` and `canvas_h` to the graph if they differ from 92% of the viewport ([state.rs:323-344](../../src/ui/state.rs#L323)). That write triggers `use_autosave`. The end-to-end test runs without a viewport, so it cannot see this.
sections.Decision: Should a saved canvas size be respected on open (set `canvas_user_set` when the loaded canvas is not the default), or is re-fitting to the window wanted? The spec's sentence says the former.

entries.title: The size-conflict dialog hides the next conflict
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Kind: Defect (small). Derived from the code; not probed, because the logic lives in the dialog's button closures, which no test can call.
sections.Observed: The two resize buttons call `app.edit`, whose `after_edit` looks for the next conflict and stores it, and then call `app.conflict.set(None)` ([dialogs.rs:42-55](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L42)), erasing it. A second mismatch elsewhere in the graph is only reported after another edit.
sections.Decision: None; drop the `set(None)` (the edit already recomputes the conflict).

entries.title: Export memory is bounded for PNG files only
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [F4.2](02-editing-and-views.md#f4-2) ("renders … in bands (to bound memory)"), [Q3](06-quality.md#q3) ("exports must run in bounded memory").
sections.Observed: Every format is *rendered* in bands, but only `Png::encode` streams them ([formats.rs:135-149](../../src/formats.rs#L135)). `ImageCrate::encode`, used for JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP and TIFF, appends every band to `all`, a buffer of the whole image, then encodes into a second in-memory buffer `buf` ([formats.rs:83-110](../../src/formats.rs#L83)). JPEG also builds an RGB copy (`rgb`). Exports to memory, used on the web, hold the whole encoded file even for PNG (`ExportDest::Memory`) ([worker.rs:311-315](../../src/worker.rs#L311)).
sections.Consequence, derived from the code: A 16384² JPEG export holds about 1 GiB of RGBA plus 768 MiB of RGB plus the encoded file in memory at once. The 16K tests export PNG only, so nothing catches this.
sections.Decision: Either stream the other encoders (JPEG and TIFF can be written in strips) or narrow the spec: "bounded memory for PNG; other formats need memory proportional to the image".

entries.title: Quick-mode work can be lost without confirmation
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [P7](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p7): "Leaving a quick-mode session that has work in it asks for confirmation."
sections.Observed: The menu's End quick session and opening a project ask through `platform::confirm`, which returns `true` without asking outside desktop ([platform.rs:217-236](../../src/ui/platform.rs#L217)); this matters on mobile, since the web has no Project menu. Nothing intercepts closing the window or quitting: `launch` sets no close behaviour ([mod.rs:26-38](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L26)), and no close-request or `beforeunload` handler exists in `src/`.
sections.Consequence: On every platform, closing the window discards quick-mode work silently. On the web, where *all* work is quick mode ([X2](04-sessions-and-projects.md#x2)), so does reloading the page.
sections.Decision: Does "leaving" include quitting? If so, desktop needs a close handler and the web a `beforeunload` prompt. If not, the spec should say "ending a quick-mode session from the Project menu".

entries.title: Platform gaps beyond the accepted ones
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [R2](01-product-and-platform.md#r2), [R3](01-product-and-platform.md#r3), [O5](03-operators.md#o5). The spec accepts only the *project* limitations ([X3](04-sessions-and-projects.md#x3)).
sections.Observed:
- The `web` feature enables neither `gpu` nor `native`, and only `desktop` enables `rembg` ([Cargo.toml:6-13](../../Cargo.toml#L6)). The web build therefore renders on the CPU, single-threaded (background jobs run through `spawn_local`) ([worker.rs:417-425](../../src/worker.rs#L417)), and has no background removal; mobile has GPU but no background removal (the stub `compute_mask`) ([bgremove.rs:169-172](../../src/nodes/bgremove.rs#L169)).
- The README says the mobile build "compiles, but it has not been run on a device". No test covers web or mobile.
sections.Decision: Extend the spec's "accepted for now" list to these gaps, or schedule them. GPU on the web needs asynchronous readback; threads need cross-origin isolation (README, Known gaps).

entries.title: Downscaling filters are not what they say
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [O8](03-operators.md#o8): "Allows choosing upscale/downscale algorithm to use." Also [O4](03-operators.md#o4), Downscale's "box" method.
sections.Observed:
When the request is at least as coarse as the input, or the input is size-less, `Resize::render` returns the area-filtered input whatever the `filter` says; only "nearest" changes the result ([resize.rs:88-98](../../src/nodes/resize.rs#L88)). Bilinear, bicubic and Fourier downscales are identical.
Downscale's "box" method is the source pyramid: for factors below 2, `level_for` returns level 0, sampled nearest, so "box" equals "nearest"; above 2 it uses a power-of-two level, not a box over the factor; size-less inputs are point-sampled ([source.rs:114-133](../../src/engine/source.rs#L114)).
sections.Decision: Keep one downscaler and say so in the spec and the UI, or implement the filters for downscaling. Today the inspector offers four Resize choices where three behave identically, and a Downscale "box" that is not a box for small factors.

entries.title: Overlay mapping: one path, affine maps only
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [F3.3.1](02-editing-and-views.md#f3-3-1): controls "must be placed correctly even when nodes between the edited node and the shown image move or scale pixels".
sections.Observed: `space_map_rec` returns the *first* path from the shown node to the edited node, trying ports in order ([graph.rs:318-343](../../src/graph.rs#L318)). Maps are separable affine `Map2`s ([geom.rs:95-102](../../src/engine/geom.rs#L95)); `Reflect` keeps the default identity `input_map` although it mirrors pixels.
sections.Consequence, derived from the code:
- If the edited node reaches the shown image twice, for example as `stack(clip(photo), photo)`, its controls follow only the first route (here, through the Clip). There is no single correct placement in that case.
- Controls of a node upstream of a Reflection are placed for the unmirrored half only.
sections.Decision: What should the view do when a node appears in the shown image more than once, or through a fold: draw every instance, draw the first and say so, or refuse? The spec's "placed correctly" does not say.

entries.title: Project errors without a column
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [E11](05-expressions.md#e11) ("Errors are reported with a line and column"), [P14](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p14).
sections.Observed: `Project::verify` reports a missing or unsafe image as `project.delos, line N: …`, formatting `pos.line` only, although `pos.col` is known ([project.rs:218-223](../../src/project.rs#L218)).
sections.Decision: Add the column (one line each), or limit the spec to syntax and semantic errors.

entries.title: Only the layer stack has a display modality
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [F5](02-editing-and-views.md#f5): "Delos shall define specific "display modalities" for standard operators".
sections.Observed: The layer stack is the only operator with a dedicated presentation (graph view rows `stack_chain`, the inspector's `LayerStack`, the `(stack …)` syntax) ([graph_view.rs:75-87](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L75)). Chains of Blend nodes, or a split and its recombination, are drawn as plain nodes.
sections.Decision: Is the stack the only modality the spec wants (its only example), or should other operators get one? If more are wanted, which: blend chains as layer stacks with per-layer modes, a split and its re-stack as a "selection"?

entries.title: Default export while editing on the input
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [F4](02-editing-and-views.md#f4): by default, "export the output currently visible in image view".
sections.Observed: When a Clip or a split is selected with "Preview selection" on, the view shows the node's *input* with its controls, but Export exports the node's *output*: `export_target` is the edited node when the view is not locked ([state.rs:380](../../src/ui/state.rs#L380)). The field's doc comment says this is intended (`Displayed`) ([state.rs:90-92](../../src/ui/state.rs#L90)).
sections.Decision: The code's choice is defensible (nobody wants to export the uncropped image while cropping), but it contradicts the spec's wording. Update one of them.

entries.title: Importing replaces what feeds the output
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Clauses: [F1.1](02-editing-and-views.md#f1-1): an import creates a Static Image "connected directly to the output".
sections.Observed: `finish_import` connects each new image to the output's only port, replacing the previous connection; the earlier node stays in the graph, detached ([mod.rs:264-268](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L264)). Importing several files at once leaves the last one connected.
sections.Decision: The spec is followed literally, but with a second import it destroys the composition feeding the output. Alternatives: connect the first import only, or add later imports as layers of a stack (the code already supports `ImportTarget::StackLayer`).

entries.title: Derived image parameters are not written
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Observed: A static image's `image`, `width` and `height` parameters are skipped when printing and rejected when reading (`IMAGE_DERIVED`) ([expr.rs:35-36](../../src/expr.rs#L35), [expr.rs:355-358](../../src/expr.rs#L355)), because they are derived from the file.
sections.Decision: None needed beyond noting the exception in the spec: these are hidden, derived values, not user parameters.

entries.title: Spec wording that cannot hold as written
entries.area: Findings: where the code and the spec disagree

sections.Observed:
- [N1](03-operators.md#n1): generators "should act as generators of data which can be input to other generators", but the previous sentence says they take no inputs. The code reads "other operators".
- [F5](02-editing-and-views.md#f5): a layer stack "will never be empty", yet the inspector offers "+ Empty slot" and an empty slot is a `None` layer (`push(None)`) ([inspector.rs:523](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L523)). The chain itself is never empty, so no NIL node is needed, which is the spec's point; the wording invites confusion.
- [O4](03-operators.md#o4): "Downscale operator - should allow for downscaling" is a sentence fragment, and Resize already downscales. The code gives Downscale a factor from 1 to 64 and a box or nearest method. The spec does not say how the two should differ.
- [P2](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p2): projects are "for sharing and collaborating with others"; only sharing archives exists. Collaboration needs a definition before it can be traced.
sections.Decision: Reword these four places so that each states something the code can be checked against.

entries.title: Undo and redo
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Every edit is an undo step holding a full copy of the graph; slider and handle drags within one second share a step; the history keeps 60 steps. ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z and ⌘Y undo and redo.
sections.Where: `HISTORY_LIMIT` and `push_history` ([state.rs:142](../../src/ui/state.rs#L142), [state.rs:179-187](../../src/ui/state.rs#L179)); `edit` and `edit_coalesced` ([state.rs:190-215](../../src/ui/state.rs#L190)); `undo` and `redo` ([state.rs:262-284](../../src/ui/state.rs#L262)); the toolbar buttons ([mod.rs:395-396](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L395)).
sections.Why it matters: The spec mentions undo only to say it is not part of a project ([P11](04-sessions-and-projects.md#p11)). Its depth and memory cost (each step may keep decoded images alive) are product decisions. Undo also caused the identity defect [D-STALE](findings.md#d-stale).

entries.title: Keyboard shortcuts
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: ⌘E exports, Delete or Backspace deletes the selection, Escape closes the export dialog or prompt or clears the selection, F fits the image.

entries.title: Adding and deleting nodes rewire the graph
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: "Add node" inserts the new node after the selected one, taking over its consumers; with nothing selected it feeds an empty output. Deleting a node with one input bridges its input to its consumers; deleting a layer stack deletes the whole chain.
sections.Why it matters: These rules decide what a user's graph looks like after the two most common edits, and they caused [D-ADD-AFTER-SPLIT](findings.md#d-add-after-split).

entries.title: The inspector beyond parameters
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Nodes can be renamed (the title becomes `:title`); every input port has a picker listing all outputs that would not form a cycle; each node shows its size, description, "slow" hint and last error.
sections.Where: The title field, which sets `label` ([inspector.rs:104-118](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L104)), input pickers built from `candidates` ([inspector.rs:160-188](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L160)), `slow_hint` ([inspector.rs:124-129](../../src/ui/inspector.rs#L124)).

entries.title: How previews are produced
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Previews render only the visible region at screen resolution, capped at 10 Mpx (`MAX_PREVIEW_PIXELS`); a newer request cancels an older one; when renders are slow a quarter-resolution frame is shown first; frames are composited over a checkerboard and sent to the webview as BMP.
sections.Where: The request effect ([image_view.rs:83-125](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L83)) and `MAX_PREVIEW_PIXELS` ([image_view.rs:15-16](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L15)); latest-wins and progressive refinement in `run_preview` ([worker.rs:179-225](../../src/worker.rs#L179)); `encode_display_bmp` ([worker.rs:449-485](../../src/worker.rs#L449)).
sections.Why it matters: This is how Delos meets the INSTRUCTIONS' "effectively instant" principle, which the spec turns into a single test clause ([Q3](06-quality.md#q3)). The 80 ms threshold and the 10 Mpx cap are unrecorded tuning decisions.

entries.title: GPU memory policy
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Source image levels are kept on the GPU up to 4 GiB (1 GiB on mobile) and evicted least recently used first; idle textures and readback buffers are pooled up to 512 MiB (128 MiB on mobile); every kernel is compiled at start-up; opt-in profiling times every operation.
sections.Why it matters: The INSTRUCTIONS ask for minimal memory use; these budgets are where that principle became numbers. `NEXT_FEATURES.md` plans to expose them in a settings menu.

entries.title: The expensive-result cache
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Background-removal masks are cached in a 256 MiB LRU keyed by structural hash; nothing else is cached.

entries.title: Operator parameters the spec does not name
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Reflection's direction (`side`); Blend's `opacity` and five extra modes; Resize's exact-size mode; Downscale's `method`; Background Removal's `invert`, `resolution` and `model`; every generator's parameters (colours, seeds, octaves, zoom, palette).
sections.Why it matters: Saved projects write every parameter ([E8](05-expressions.md#e8)), so each of these names and defaults is now part of the file format.

entries.title: A third answer to a size conflict
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Besides resizing one input ([Z1](03-operators.md#z1)), the user can keep both sizes, aligned top-left; the answer is remembered per node and pair of sizes.

entries.title: Image formats
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: PNG, JPEG, WebP (lossless), GIF, BMP and TIFF are read and written; ICO is read only; JPEG exports are composited over white; JPEG quality is adjustable.
sections.Where: `CODECS` ([formats.rs:152-164](../../src/formats.rs#L152)); the JPEG branch of `ImageCrate::encode` ([formats.rs:91-102](../../src/formats.rs#L91)); the export dialog's format and `quality` fields ([dialogs.rs:129-169](../../src/ui/dialogs.rs#L129)).
sections.Why it matters: The INSTRUCTIONS ask for "most common web formats" with an extensible design; the spec says nothing about formats. AVIF is missing (README).

entries.title: Where exports go
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Desktop asks with a save dialog; mobile writes to `~/Documents` without asking; the web downloads the file.

entries.title: Errors and progress shown in place
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: A failing node is marked in the graph view and its error shown in the image view and the inspector; long steps (Fourier resampling, the neural network) show a status line; imports show a spinner.

entries.title: Choosing the backend at run time
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: `DELOS_NO_GPU` forces the CPU; the toolbar badge switches between GPU and CPU for the session.

entries.title: Navigating the views
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: The image view zooms with the wheel, pans by dragging, and has Fit (also double-click) and 1:1; the graph view pans, zooms, has Home, and lets wires be dragged, picked up and selected.
sections.Where: Image view handlers (`onwheel`, `Drag::Pan`) ([image_view.rs:207-244](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L207)) and its status bar buttons, Fit, 1:1 and `zoom_by` ([image_view.rs:340-358](../../src/ui/image_view.rs#L340)); graph view handlers (`GDrag`) ([graph_view.rs:256-295](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L256)) and tools ([graph_view.rs:432-455](../../src/ui/graph_view.rs#L432)).

entries.title: Layer stacks grow from the inspector
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Besides disabling and removing ([O1.1](03-operators.md#o1-1)), layers can be reordered, and the inspector adds image layers, generator layers and empty slots.

entries.title: Session housekeeping
entries.area: Unspecified behaviour: code without a spec clause

sections.What: Session stashes older than a day are deleted at start-up; a new project's name must not collide with a non-empty folder; the window title shows the project or mode; "Close project" starts over.
sections.Where: `new_stash_dir` ([worker.rs:399-415](../../src/worker.rs#L399)); the collision check in `create_project` ([session.rs:156-161](../../src/ui/session.rs#L156)); the title effect (`set_title`) ([mod.rs:62-70](../../src/ui/mod.rs#L62)); `close_session` ([session.rs:218-223](../../src/ui/session.rs#L218)).

spec_units.section: Delos - a generative image editing tool
spec_units.text: Delos is to be an image editing tool focused on combining existing content with generative content.

spec_units.section: Delos - a generative image editing tool
spec_units.text: By generative content, we mean both AI-generated content and traditionally generative content, using classical procedural generation algorithms.
Delos must be built using the Rust programming language.
Delos must be possible to run as a desktop application, a web-based application and a mobile application.
We would like to use Dioxus as our framework for this purpose.
Delos will extensively display and manipulate images.
Using GPU acceleration wherever possible is a requirement for this project.
However, in case GPU acceleration is not available, Delos should degrade gracefully to CPU rendering.
Delos must be able to load and display existing images.
Opening an image creates a "layer" containing that image.
Layers are treated as graph nodes which can be connected using "operators".
Importing an image to Delos specifically creates a "Static Image" node connected directly to the output.
Operators may have parameters.
In case they do, adding the operator node will allow the user to input the operator parameters either via a WYSIWYG interface or via form inputs.
While an image is being edited in Delos, we will be able to visualize the final results.
During the process of editing, however, the image will be stored as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) representing image layers and operations applied to them.
That way, we can easily see and modify effects are being applied to which parts of the image.
The image view must show the image that is being sent to the output.
We must be able to open a graph view instead of the image view or alongside the image view.
It must also be possible to visualize any part of the graph which produces an image.
In other terms, we can temporarily relocate the output to any image node.
Double-clicking a node in the graph view relocates the output to it.
For nodes with several outputs, double-clicking one of its output ports relocates the output to that output.
Double-clicking the relocated node again, or the Output node, moves the output back to its default.
If we select an operator node, the image view should show the image at the operator's output overlaid with controls for the specific operator (examples of controls: selection boxes, rules).
Examples are given in the operators section below.
Some operators are edited on their input instead.
For example, Clip shows the uncropped input with the crop rectangle.
It must be possible to keep the image view fixed while editing a node further up the graph.
While the output is relocated (or when "Preview selection" is turned off), selecting another node keeps the view as it is and draws that node's controls over the shown image.
Editing those controls modifies the shown image directly.
Controls must be placed correctly even when nodes between the edited node and the shown image move or scale pixels (Clip, Resize, Downscale, …).
Every node type describes how it maps coordinates to its inputs, so new node types can take part.
If the selected node does not contribute to the shown image, the view says so instead of showing controls.
It must be possible to export the image output by any Delos image operator, but by default the easiest operation to perform should be to export the output currently visible in image view.
While the output is relocated, exporting the current image will export the content of the node that is currently attached to output.
Export renders at full resolution in bands (to bound memory), shows progress and can be cancelled.
The export dialog can be closed with its close button, the Escape key or by clicking outside it, and closes by itself after a successful export.
All combinations of images will be done using operators.
For example, rather than stacking layers by default, Delos should make it possible to combine layers with specific operators.

Delos shall define specific "display modalities" for standard operators to make user experience more pleasurable - for example, if we combine a sequence of layers using the "stack" operator, we can display this as a layer stack rather than as a degenerate graph of the format `(layer3 STACK (layer2 STACK layer1))` (i.e. a Lisp list of stacks, with the exception that it will never be empty hence a NIL-node is not required.)
These are basic layer operators which must be implemented in the initial version of Delos:
Stack operator - this is a basic operator which is used to form layer stacks.
A layer stack will be internally represented as `(frontmost STACK (second-frontmost STACK (third-frontmost STACK ... (second-backmost STACK last) ... )))`.
A layer stack will show the first non-transparent pixel found along the stack for each position.
Delos implements this as standard "over" alpha compositing: this matches the rule for opaque pixels and also handles partly transparent ones.
Takes no parameters.

If the stack operator is selected it should allow editing the stack, for example temporarily disabling inputs (which will be internally represented as a "Disable" operator which changes all pixels to transparent) or removing them completely.
Disable operator - mentioned with stack above.
Simple reflection operator - this should allow making reflections, i.e. placing axes of reflection on the image which will copy the pixels to one side of them to the other side.
This tool, when selected, will allow (via WYSIWYG rule or form input) selecting where to position the axis of reflection.
Via form, it should allow selecting a vertical or horizontal axis of reflection.
It should also allow specifying whether the reflection should be additive, subtractive or replace the pixels where the reflection will fall.
Downscale operator - should allow for downscaling
Background removal operator - this should allow removing the input image's background using the `rembg-rs` crate.
Controls set the background removal parameters.
Invert operator - inverts colors.
No controls.
Clip - allows selecting a subset of image.
Resize - allows upscaling or downscaling input.
Allows choosing upscale/downscale algorithm to use.
Should offer nearest-neighbor, bilinear, bicubic and fourier-based interpolation.
Blend operator - allows combining images with the blend modes specified at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blend_modes plus the following:
Logic Gate: applies logic operation (and, or, xor) to both images.
Note that nand, nor and xnor are not included bc they can be achieved with the invert operator.
Splitting an image produces two output images, one for each side of a split border.
One output contains the pixels on one side of the border, with every pixel on the other side transparent.
The other output contains the complementary pixels, with those present in the first output transparent.
This makes localized effects possible, as selections do in a regular editor.
Vertical Split (`left` / `right`), Horizontal Split (`top` / `bottom`) and Rectangle Split (`inside` / `outside`) are provided.
Each is controlled in the image view by dragging the border line, or by moving and resizing the rectangle, or via form inputs.
Exact partition: every pixel belongs to exactly one output, decided by its centre.
Stacking the two outputs therefore reproduces the input exactly, at any zoom level.
Editing view: when a split is selected, the image view shows its whole input with the border controls.
Outputs: the inputs of other nodes, the relocated output and exports can each refer to a specific output of a split.
Size: splits keep their input's size, and splitting a size-less (generative) input splits it at whatever size is requested.
Extensibility: nodes in general may have any number of outputs.
Each node type declares its outputs, and every output of a node has the node's size.
These operators are differentiated by not taking any inputs.
Rather, they should act as generators of data which can be input to other generators.
Note that generative operators do not have output size - if they are connected directly to output, the user must specify the desired output size (this should be possible to do via WYSIWYG).
The output size which fits naturally into the current Delos window should be selected by default.
If generative operators are connected to combining operators, they will generate at whatever size is necessary to combine successfully with the other side.
The initial generators are: solid color, linear gradient, radial gradient, checkerboard, noise (fBm, turbulence, ridged), Voronoi and Mandelbrot.
An AI image-generation operator is planned.
As said above, generative operators should generate at the size required of them and should not specify an output size.
However, the outputs produced by imported images and by combining operators will have a definite size.
In this case, Delos should ask which output size must be used and insert a resizing node after one of the inputs as appropriate.
Delos supports two ways of working:
Quick mode is for one-off edits and quick work.
Imported images are used where they are and nothing is saved.
Project mode is for longer-term work, and for sharing and collaborating with others.
When the user imports an image and neither a project nor a quick-mode session is open, Delos asks whether to create a project.
The question makes clear that projects copy every imported image, so they take more storage.
If the user declines, a quick-mode session starts and later imports are added to it without asking again.
If the user accepts, a project is created (named by the user; by default in `~/.delos/projects/<name>`, overridable with `DELOS_PROJECTS_DIR`) and the image is added to it.
The current work can also be turned into a project at any time ("New project from current work").
The images the graph uses are copied into it.
The bottom of the window always shows whether Delos is in quick mode or in a project (with its name and location), and whether the project's changes are saved.
Projects are saved automatically after every change.
Saves are atomic, so a project file is never left half-written.
Opening a project does not change anything on disk until the user edits it.
Leaving a quick-mode session that has work in it asks for confirmation.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: A project is a directory:

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: <name>/ project.delos the node graph, as a Delos expression (see below) inputs/ copies of the images the graph uses

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: Imported images are copied into `inputs/` unchanged (no re-encoding) when their original bytes are available.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: Images known only by their pixels are written as PNG.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: `inputs/` contains exactly the images the current graph uses.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: Images that are no longer used are removed from it.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: Undo history is not part of a project.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: It belongs to the editing session and is not expected to survive closing and reopening a project.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: Within a session, images the history may still need are kept outside the project (in a temporary session folder).

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Project structure
spec_units.text: If an undo brings an image back, it is copied back into `inputs/` unchanged.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: Share Project exports the current project as a `.delosproject` file: a zip archive containing the project directory.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: Import Project accepts a `.delosproject` file, a `project.delos` file or a project directory.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: A `.delosproject` file is unpacked into the projects folder under a new name, so it never overwrites an existing project.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: A directory is opened in place, without copying.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: Projects can also be opened by dropping them onto the window.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: Before opening, Delos verifies the structure:

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: `project.delos` exists and parses;

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: `inputs/` exists;

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: every image the graph refers to exists inside `inputs/`.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: It reports precisely what is wrong otherwise.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: Paths that would point outside the project, whether in the project file or inside an archive, are rejected.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Sharing and importing projects
spec_units.text: A failed import leaves nothing behind.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: The node graph has a plain-text representation, so we can speak of Delos *expressions*.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: It is a Lisp-like format, in keeping with layer stacks being treated as non-empty lists:

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: ; Nodes used more than once are bound with def; everything else nests. (def photo (image "inputs/photo.png" :at (60 40))) (output (stack (invert photo) (blend photo (noise :scale 0.3) :mode screen)) :canvas_w 1920 :canvas_h 1080) (noise :seed 4) ; nodes not connected to anything are kept too

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: A node is written `(kind input… :param value…)`.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: Inputs come in port order, and `_` leaves a port empty.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: Nodes with several outputs (splits) are always bound with `def`, and each output is referred to as `name.output`, e.g. `s.left`.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: `(stack front … back)` is a layer stack.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: `(image "inputs/…")` is a static image.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: `:at (x y)` is a node's position in the graph view, and `:title "…"` gives it a custom title.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: Values are numbers, `true`/`false`, choices as symbols, colors as `(r g b a)` lists and text as strings.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: Comments start with `;`.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: When saving, every parameter is written, including defaults, so a project keeps its meaning if a default changes later.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: When reading, omitted parameters take their defaults, and nodes without `:at` are laid out automatically, so expressions can be written by hand.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: Serializing and deserializing must be fast.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: Doing both must give a functionally identical graph: the same nodes, connections, parameters, titles and positions, rendering the same pixels.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Delos expressions
spec_units.text: Errors are reported with a line and column.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Platform status
spec_units.text: Projects are currently desktop-first:

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Platform status
spec_units.text: Mobile supports projects but has no file pickers yet, so Import and Share Project are unavailable there.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Platform status
spec_units.text: Web has no file system and always works in quick mode.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Platform status
spec_units.text: These limitations are accepted for now.

spec_units.section: Sessions: quick mode and projects / Platform status
spec_units.text: Full functionality on all platforms is a later goal.
Bugs that are fixed must get regression tests that reproduce them.
Project features must be covered by unit tests and by end-to-end tests.
The end-to-end tests run the application's real state, background worker and autosave without a window, and drive them as the user interface does.
Performance at 16K resolution is tested: previews must stay interactive, and exports must run in bounded memory.
